manifest.prompt: make me a metadump for the luminous chromatic translucency aesthetic: transparent blue acrylic and vinyl, overexposed blue-tinted whites, hyperreal electric green grass under a saturated blue sky, frutiger aero / y2k translucency vibes. colors should feel like they exist inside the material, not painted on. i want to use it for image generation and later for a landing page
manifest.built: lite smoke test of the metadump skill: prompt shard (main loop); research x1; specialists x3 + exclusion; synthesis + build; dry-run verify x2 (of 7 routes); remaining tier-2 guesses recorded as open questions; no gap round at lite depth.
how_to_read: 1. Read the head first: the first 31 lines hold manifest, essence and routing (Read limit=31, or jq '{manifest, essence, routing}' luminous-translucency.metadump.json).
2. Pick the route for your job and run its jq: jq '<routing[i].jq>' luminous-translucency.metadump.json
3. Also pull what constrains your scope: jq '.anti_keywords, .checks' luminous-translucency.metadump.json
4. Look up any term (lowercase): jq '.index["<term>"]' luminous-translucency.metadump.json  -> hits give id + path; not_meant lists senses to avoid.
5. Grep works too: every entry is one line, so grep -n '<word>' luminous-translucency.metadump.json returns whole entries.

essence.one_sentence: Saturated blue that lives inside transparent acrylic and vinyl because daylight passes through it, set in a high-key world of blooming blue-white light, hyperreal electric-green grass and a deep clear sky: Frutiger Aero and Y2K translucency, rebuilt from optics rather than copied from its artifacts.

poles: whites pushed to near-clipping blue-white bloom
sky, grass and deep material blue held at full saturation
clear enough to see into and through the body
deep saturated blue wherever light travels far through it
grass and sky more vivid and cleaner than life
plausible optics: refraction, absorption with depth, caustics, tinted shadows
Frutiger Aero and Y2K translucency lineage
no Bliss recreation, OS chrome, iMac copies or meme collage
translucent, softly blurred panels over a real scene
the color carried by tint depth, lit edges and blue spill, not white frost

generic.positive: {subject}, made of transparent blue acrylic and translucent blue vinyl, set in hyperreal electric-green grass under a deep, saturated blue sky. The color lives inside the material: pale clear blue where it is thin, deep sapphire through its thickest parts and where layers overlap, polished edges glowing bright saturated blue, crisp white highlights on the surface. A high sun behind the object shines through it, laying a blue-tinted shadow and bright caustic light on the grass and a white surface beside it. Overexposed blue-tinted whites bloom softly around highlights and small cloud tops while the sky and grass stay fully saturated. Calm open fields, low camera, Frutiger Aero and Y2K translucency.
generic.constraints: Constraints: (1) the blue deepens with thickness and overlap, never one flat blue on the object; (2) highlights are white over the blue body, and shadows under the material are blue light with caustics, never grey; (3) only whites and highlight cores bloom or clip, sky, grass and deep blue stay saturated, no haze over the frame; (4) neutral-white daylight, azure-to-cobalt blue (never aqua), real vivid grass (never olive or turf); (5) an original scene with no logos, window chrome, lettering or people.
generic.negative: painted surface, flat color fill, frosted glass, grey shadow, golden hour, washed-out sky, haze, neon, vaporwave, holographic, artificial turf, text

params.default_subject: a thick rounded slab of transparent blue acrylic

generic.notes: {subject} is open (q-ml-subject): the default is a simple original form (slab, sphere, ring, sheet, inflatable). Choices a user may vary: aspect (q-ml-aspect), camera (cam-ml-lens-angle), time of day (q-pe-time-of-day), exact hex ramps (pal-*, proposed, not measured). Real references (Bliss, Windows, iMac, Apple) stay out of the prompt by default (q-named-refs-in-prompts). FLUX and other models without a negative field: drop 'negative'; gpt-image and Gemini: append the constraints line; SD: use 'negative' as written; Midjourney: --no with single words only.

variants.name: blue hour (tier 4, optional)
variants.positive: Just after sunset: a cobalt sky deepening overhead to clear azure at the horizon, no orange or pink band. The last bright sky shines through {subject} of transparent blue acrylic, making it the brightest thing in the frame, cut edges glowing saturated blue inside blue-white bloom; deep green grass turns electric only where the transmitted light spills onto it.

variants.name: shallow sunlit water (tier 4, optional)
variants.positive: Shallow sunlit water seen from below: a bright blue-white water surface overhead with a sharp circle of sun, clear blue water deepening with distance, {subject} of translucent blue acrylic among electric-green seagrass, a net of near-white caustic lines moving across everything. Clean blue, never turquoise or murky.

tokens.notes: Starting values (status: illustrative), not a spec. Use one open-license humanist sans (p-lp-type-candidates) unless the brand has its own (q-lp-brand-fonts). Recompute contrast with a-lp-contrast-pairs after changing any color token; --acrylic-body is for alpha tints only (white text on it is 3.5:1).

brief.text: Must: every translucent surface (nav, panels, cards, CTAs, hero object) is a tinted blue slab whose tint deepens toward its lower rim and where panels overlap, lit by one shared light: near-white top edge, glowing bottom edge, blue light spilling onto the surface below. Page whites are blue-tinted (#F6FAFF page, #EAF4FF plates). The hero is an original saturated sky over electric-green grass with one acrylic object. Should: backdrop blur only on the nav and one or two hero panels, over a real scene; full optical treatment only on the hero object and primary CTAs; humanist sans, 24px card radii, pill CTAs; one specular sweep with a reduced-motion fallback. Say instead: tinted acrylic, not white frosted glassmorphism; alpha in backgrounds, not opacity on panels that hold text; blue light spill, not grey drop shadows; one curved reflection per pill, not Web 2.0 clip-art gloss; original shapes, not OS window chrome. Text: navy ink on plates or light sky, white only high on the zenith or on deep blue, never bright green as text. Unknowns: product, copy, hero media and stack are open; defaults are a consumer tech launch page, placeholder copy, a generated still hero, and static HTML/CSS.

ak-painted-on.instead: color carried inside the material: tint that deepens with thickness and glows at thin edges as light passes through
ak-painted-on.note: the instead wording is the builder's rewrite of the user's 'not painted on'

ak-chromecore.instead: tinted translucent plastic and clear blue acrylic whose color lives inside the material, with light passing through
ak-chromecore.trigger: the word 'y2k' in a prompt pulls models toward chrome and metallic finishes

ak-ml-tinted-highlights.instead: white or pale sky-blue specular highlights sitting on the surface, with the blue visible beneath them
ak-ml-tinted-highlights.trigger: 'shiny blue' or 'glossy blue' pulls models toward metallic or anodized finishes where the highlight itself turns blue

ak-ml-warm-halation.instead: cool blue-white bloom held close around the brightest highlights
ak-ml-warm-halation.trigger: asking for 'halation' or a 'film look' brings the red-orange halos film stock produces around highlights

ak-ml-grey-shadows.instead: a blue-tinted transmitted shadow, deepest under the thickest parts, with bright caustic lines or a bright core
ak-ml-grey-shadows.trigger: product-shot defaults add a neutral contact shadow as if the object were opaque

ak-pe-washed-sky.instead: a deep, saturated blue sky held at full color while only whites, cloud tops and specular cores bloom
ak-pe-washed-sky.trigger: 'overexposed' in the prompt pulls models toward raising the whole exposure, which bleaches the sky first

ak-pe-warm-light.instead: clear high daylight in neutral white with blue skylight filling the shadows, so whites and shadows lean faintly blue
ak-pe-warm-light.trigger: 'luminous', 'overexposed' and nostalgic associations pull models toward warm, hazy golden light

ak-pe-aqua-drift.instead: a clean azure-to-cobalt blue (hue about 205-228°) through the whole thickness ramp, pale #B9E0FF to deep #0A43B0, with the most saturated blue at polished edges
ak-pe-aqua-drift.trigger: 'transparent', 'acrylic' and glass defaults pull models toward greenish glass edges and tropical turquoise, which merges the blue into the green grass

ak-lp-pure-white-page.instead: blue-tinted whites from the white ramp (#F6FAFF page, #EAF4FF plates, #DDEDFF bands) with soft bloom around the light sources; pure #FFFFFF only in small speculars
ak-lp-pure-white-page.trigger: web templates and component libraries default to #FFFFFF page backgrounds

ak-lp-grey-drop-shadow.instead: colored light spill: a blurred blue glow pooling beneath each translucent object, plus a small faint core-blue contact shadow
ak-lp-grey-drop-shadow.trigger: default component libraries ship neutral elevation shadows

ak-lp-web20-clipart-gloss.instead: one curved reflection per pill or hero object, from the page's single light and kept above the label, with crisp flat-lit type
ak-lp-web20-clipart-gloss.trigger: 'frutiger aero' and 'web 2.0' pull in the period's decorative gloss tropes along with its light

ak-acrylic-paint.excluded_sense: acrylic paint and acrylic painting (canvas, brushstrokes, acrylic pour, fluid art); acrylic nails; acrylic yarn or fabric
ak-acrylic-paint.instead: clear acrylic plastic (PMMA, plexiglass): cast blocks, sheets and molded shapes tinted blue through their whole thickness, transmitting and refracting light
ak-acrylic-paint.trigger: 'blue acrylic' without 'transparent', 'block' or 'sheet' drifts to paint

ak-acrylic-fluent.excluded_sense: only the UI 'Acrylic' brush of Microsoft Fluent Design: a pale, blurred, noise-textured backdrop with no tint that deepens with thickness
ak-acrylic-fluent.instead: the physical tinted acrylic, translated to the page as a blue tint that varies across the surface, a bright edge, inner glow and color spill; backdrop blur is at most one ingredient

ak-vinyl-siding.excluded_sense: vinyl siding, flooring and wallpaper; cut-vinyl decals and stickers; opaque designer vinyl toys and figures; black vinyl records; faux-leather vinyl upholstery
ak-vinyl-siding.instead: translucent tinted PVC you can see light through: transparent blue records, clear tinted vinyl sheet and film, inflatable clear vinyl

ak-frutiger-typeface.excluded_sense: the Frutiger typeface or its designer as the subject: type-specimen posters, the word set in type, or a requirement to license and use that font
ak-frutiger-typeface.instead: Frutiger Aero, the c. 2004-2013 consumer-tech aesthetic of sky, grass and glassy materials; on the page a humanist sans is an optional lineage, not the Frutiger font

ak-y2k-bug.excluded_sense: the Y2K millennium software bug: 1999-to-2000 countdowns, crashing computers, '2000' date text, doomsday imagery
ak-y2k-bug.instead: the late-1990s/early-2000s design look: tinted see-through plastic casings and clear accents in rounded blobject forms

ak-translucency-opacity.excluded_sense: a UI opacity or alpha value alone: a layer simply faded, or set to opacity 0.x
ak-translucency-opacity.instead: optical light transmission through a tinted body: light enters, deepens in blue with path length, scatters into an inner glow, refracts what is behind, and leaves bright edges and blue light spill

ak-overexposed-ruined.excluded_sense: a failed exposure: clipped, detail-less whites, a blown-out sky, washed-out grey colors and flat contrast
ak-overexposed-ruined.instead: deliberate high-key whites held just below clipping, faintly blue, blooming softly only at the brightest edges and highlights, while the blues and greens stay deep and saturated

ak-blue-tint-cast.excluded_sense: a blue or cyan grade over the whole frame (cool white balance, blue filter, teal-and-orange), which turns the grass teal and the sky grey-cyan
ak-blue-tint-cast.instead: only the whites and highlights lean faintly blue; the grass keeps its own vivid green, the sky its own saturated blue, and the acrylic carries the deepest blue

ak-chromatic-rainbow.excluded_sense: rainbow or multi-hue color: chromatic aberration, RGB channel split, prism-rainbow dispersion
ak-chromatic-rainbow.instead: strongly colored: one saturated blue carried inside the material, set in a blue, white and green scene; at most a faint natural spectral fringe on a sharp edge

ak-electric-emissive.excluded_sense: electricity or emitted light: lightning, sparks, glowing or bioluminescent grass, neon or fluorescent highlighter green
ak-electric-emissive.instead: intensely vivid: real sunlit grass at a saturation beyond life, its brightness coming from daylight, with backlit blade tips glowing where light passes through them

ak-luminous-emissive.excluded_sense: self-lit: neon tubes, LEDs, lamps inside objects, glow-in-the-dark or bioluminescent materials
ak-luminous-emissive.instead: filled with daylight: brightness comes from light passing through and bouncing off the material (transmission, inner glow, bright edges, caustics, bloom on whites)

ak-hyperreal-tags.excluded_sense: the hyperrealism painting genre, or render tags like 'hyper-realistic 8K ultra-detailed' that give over-sharpened, uncanny CGI
ak-hyperreal-tags.instead: heightened realism: more saturated and clearer than life, the way vivid daylight film renders it, while staying physically plausible

ak-transparent-background.excluded_sense: a transparent background (PNG alpha cutout, checkerboard pattern, an object isolated on nothing), or a colorless object that nearly disappears
ak-transparent-background.instead: see-through tinted material inside a full scene, so its blue, refraction and light spill show against sky, grass or white

ak-generic-glassmorphism.instead: panels tinted blue from within: deeper where thicker and where panels overlap, with a bright refracted rim, soft inner glow and blue light spilling onto nearby white, set over a real sky or grass scene
ak-generic-glassmorphism.trigger: 'glass', 'translucent card' or 'frutiger aero UI' in a web or UI brief
ak-generic-glassmorphism.note: 'frosted' stays allowed for the material itself (frosted acrylic with subsurface glow); this excludes the white-fill-plus-blur card recipe, not the word

shortcut.to: white 10-30% fill + backdrop blur + 1px white border
shortcut.why: that recipe is a pale opacity effect with no color inside the material

check.spec: rgba\(\s*255\s*,\s*255\s*,\s*255\s*,\s*0?\.[0-3]\d*\s*\) in a rule that also sets backdrop-filter; a hit fails unless the same surface also layers a blue tint that varies across it and an edge highlight

good: a deep-blue acrylic panel whose tint thickens toward its lower edge, rim-lit white along the top, over a blurred sunlit sky
bad: a white frosted card with a 1px white border floating over purple gradient blobs

ak-opacity-panels.instead: keep text and content at full opacity; build translucency from layered tinted backgrounds (alpha in background colors only), edge highlights, inner glow and a backdrop blur of a real scene

check.spec: (?<![-\w])opacity\s*:\s*0?\.\d+ on any element that contains text; allowed only on decorative ::before/::after tint or highlight layers

ak-clear-glass-blue-backdrop.term: clear glass in front of blue
variants: blue rim light on clear plastic
ak-clear-glass-blue-backdrop.instead: the material itself is blue: it stays blue against white or green, deepens with thickness and at edges seen end-on, and casts blue caustics onto nearby white surfaces

shortcut.why: a clear object only borrows color from what is behind or around it; the prompt asks for color inside the material

good: a thick blue acrylic cube on white sand, its blue deepest through the corners, throwing a blue caustic pool beside it
bad: a clear crystal sphere in front of a blue studio backdrop

ak-plastic-toy.instead: optically clear or translucent blue acrylic and vinyl: refraction, tint that deepens with thickness, bright thin edges and faint internal structure visible through the body
ak-plastic-toy.note: never exclude the word 'plastic' itself: translucent plastic is the material

shortcut.why: opaque plastic carries its color on the surface, which is the painted-on look

ak-vaporwave.instead: the blue, white and green triad: saturated sky blue, faintly blue-white highlights and vivid grass green, with the deepest blue inside the acrylic
ak-vaporwave.trigger: 'y2k', 'aesthetic', 'gradient' and 'dreamy' pull toward purple-pink; landing-page defaults reach for indigo-violet gradients

ak-neon-night.instead: high-key daylight: a sunlit sky, bright grass, open shadows tinted blue; the only glow is daylight passing through the material
ak-neon-night.trigger: 'electric', 'luminous' and 'futuristic' pull toward neon and night
ak-neon-night.note: applies to the default direction; a deliberately chosen dusk or dark variant sets its own rules

ak-muddy-blues.instead: clean, saturated blues: bright sky blue overhead, a deep clear blue where the acrylic is thickest, whites bright and only faintly blue

ak-holographic.instead: a single blue hue living inside the material with clean white highlights; at most a faint spectral fringe on a sharp edge

ak-global-haze.instead: bloom only on the brightest whites and thin bright edges; the saturated fields and the material's edges stay crisp and high-contrast

ak-artificial-grass.instead: real grass blades with natural variation in length and angle, sunlit and saturated beyond life, tips glowing where backlit

shortcut.why: the intensity comes from light and saturation, not from a fake material

ak-aero-meme-collage.instead: one coherent scene: one or a few translucent blue forms in a simple sky-and-grass field, with the optical complexity concentrated where light passes through the material; bubbles, bokeh or a lens flare only when the subject calls for them, and sparingly
ak-aero-meme-collage.trigger: 'frutiger aero', 'vibes' and 'aesthetic' used as bare style tags

ak-era-pastiche.instead: original forms that borrow relationships, not artifacts: tinted see-through bodies, glossy pill controls with one top highlight, blurred panes over a real scene; no OS or product chrome, logos, product silhouettes or period props unless the subject calls for them

ak-bliss-recreation.instead: an original landscape with its own horizon line, hill shape and cloud pattern, keeping only the saturated field-under-sky relationship

ak-stock-people.instead: no people by default: the material, light and environment are the subject; if people are asked for, keep them candid and secondary to the translucent objects

ak-style-words-as-text.instead: no lettering in the image unless the subject needs it; style words steer the look and never appear in it
ak-style-words-as-text.trigger: style tags in quotes, or 'poster', 'logo' or 'title' in the prompt

ak-noise-quality-tags.note: spend the words on material, optics and light instead

ak-noise-vibes.instead: name the hues (saturated sky blue, faintly blue-white, vivid grass green) and the optical cues
ak-noise-vibes.note: 'Frutiger Aero aesthetic' as a style name is fine; bare 'aesthetic' is deliberately not listed so it is not matched inside that name

k-img-depth-tint.text: Each translucent blue object shows the same blue at clearly different depths: pale where thin, deep where thick, edge-on or overlapped.

test.spec: sample the thinnest and thickest visible part of each object: thick is about 25 L* or more darker and more saturated; every overlap is darker than either layer alone; a uniform blue fails

k-img-white-speculars.text: Highlights on the material are white or pale sky-blue, sit on the surface and follow its curve, with the blue body visible under them.

test.spec: highlight cores are near-neutral and brighter than any blue in the body; no saturated-blue or metallic highlights

k-img-light-lands.text: Light that passed through the material lands in frame as a blue shadow, caustic pool or blue spill.

test.spec: each blue object in direct light has a shadow or nearby white surface containing blue light; a neutral grey shadow under a clear blue object fails

k-img-luminous-whites.text: Whites are high-key and bloom, while saturated colors keep their saturation; clipping only at the sun and highlight cores.

test.spec: fully clipped pixels about 1-10% of the frame, all at light sources, specular cores or sunlit thin edges; deep-blue and grass regions keep HSV S of 60% or more; white areas show a pale-blue gradient, not a flat plateau

k-img-whites-blue.text: Whites lean blue and nothing in whites, shadows or sky is warm.

test.spec: in regions with lightness above 85%, mean blue channel is at or above red (8-bit, typically +8 to +40 in blooms and near the material); no region of whites or shadows has red above blue

k-img-sky.text: The sky is a deep, saturated blue gradient that stays saturated while whites bloom.

test.spec: upper third of visible sky: hue about 205-220, HSV S 55% or more, lightening smoothly toward the horizon with no banding, haze or grey

k-img-grass.text: Grass is real, dense, saturated green with a range from deep bases to glowing yellow-green tips.

test.spec: grass pixels hue 80-140 with HSV S 60% or more in lit tips and blade bodies; no olive, straw, brown or bare patches; blades vary naturally in length and angle (no uniform turf)

k-img-blue-not-aqua.text: The material blue is azure to cobalt, never aqua, turquoise or violet, and blue and green stay apart on the hue wheel.

test.spec: material pixels hue about 205-228; under 2% of the frame falls between hue 140 and 200; no pink or purple field

k-img-material.text: The material reads as transparent blue acrylic or translucent blue vinyl: tinted through its body, see-into, and blue even against white or green.

test.spec: a reviewer can see into the object (refraction or a softened view through it) and it stays blue where it crosses white or grass; an opaque glossy toy, clear glass over a blue backdrop, or acrylic paint fails

k-img-fields-focus.text: Calm simple fields take most of the frame and optical complexity gathers in one focal zone.

test.spec: low-detail sky, grass and white fields cover at least about 40% of the frame; refraction, caustics and bloom cluster in a zone of about 25% or less; the translucent body is backed by light; scattered orbs, bubbles and lens flares fail

k-img-daylight-clean.text: High-key daylight with one blue hue in the material: no neon night, vaporwave palette or holographic rainbow.

test.spec: daylit scene; no emissive neon tubes, magenta or purple gradients, or rainbow iridescence on the material

k-original.text: Forms and scenes are original: the lineage contributes relationships, not recognizable artifacts.

test.spec: no recognizable Bliss hill, OS window chrome or logos, iMac G3 shell or meme-collage props; prompts do not name Bliss, Windows, Vista, iMac or Apple

k-img-no-lettering.text: No lettering or style names appear in the image unless the subject needs them; no stock people by default.

test.spec: no rendered text such as 'Frutiger Aero' or 'Y2K'; no posed stock-photo people

k-noise-words.text: Prompts and page copy spend words on material, optics and light, not filler.

test.spec: (?i)\b(masterpiece|best quality|8k|4k|ultra[- ]detailed|highly detailed|award-winning|trending on artstation|stunning|breathtaking|gorgeous|epic|jaw-dropping|vibes|vibey|pop of color|seamless|cutting-edge|next-gen|state-of-the-art|revolutionary|world-class|elevate)\b must not match the prompt or copy

k-lp-color-inside.text: Every translucent page surface is a tinted slab: tint deeper at rim and overlap, a lit top edge, tinted light landing below.

test.spec: shown the page, a reviewer can point to where each translucent surface's blue gets deeper (rim, overlap), where light enters (top edge) and where tinted light lands (spill below); any surface that is one flat fill fails

k-lp-no-glassmorphism.text: Panels are not generic white frost: translucency comes from blue tint layers, never from element opacity.

test.spec: flag panel rules whose only fill is white alpha, e.g. background(-color)?\s*:\s*rgba\(255,\s*255,\s*255,\s*0?\.[0-4]\d*\) with no blue tint layer; and (?<![-\w])opacity\s*:\s*0?\.\d+ on any element containing text

k-lp-no-grey-shadow.text: Shadows under translucent elements are blue spill and core-blue contact shadows, never neutral grey or black.

test.spec: box-shadow values on translucent components must not match rgba\(0,\s*0,\s*0 or #000 / grey hex; use --shadow-spill and --shadow-contact

k-lp-tinted-whites.text: Page and section backgrounds are blue-tinted whites; pure white only in small speculars and text on deep blue.

test.spec: (?i)(background(-color)?)\s*:\s*(#fff(fff)?|white)\b must not match on html, body, main or section selectors

k-lp-contrast.text: All text meets WCAG contrast against its worst-case backdrop, including behind translucent layers; bright greens are never text.

test.spec: body text 4.5:1 or more and large text (24px, or 18.66px bold) 3:1 or more, measured on the worst-case composited backdrop; no body text in the #3576DA-#4E8BE0 sky band; #3DCB2A and #A8F03A never used as text color

k-lp-reduced-motion.text: Under reduced motion, sweeps, drift, parallax and lifts stop while state changes stay visible.

test.spec: emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (e.g. Playwright page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion: 'reduce'})); after load and on hover, document.getAnimations() has no running transform animation and none longer than 150ms

q-named-refs-in-prompts.text: May image prompts name the real references (Bliss, Windows Aero, iMac G3, Apple, Microsoft)?
q-named-refs-in-prompts.default: No. Use 'Frutiger Aero' and 'Y2K translucent' as style words and describe the transferable relationships; never name Bliss, Windows, Vista, iMac or Apple in image prompts, which invites recognizable copies of rights-held works.
q-named-refs-in-prompts.impact: image prompt wording and IP safety

q-ml-subject.text: What are the images of: abstract material studies, everyday or product objects made of blue acrylic or vinyl, landscapes with a material element, or UI-like icons?
q-ml-subject.default: simple original object forms (slab, sphere, rod, ring, sheet, inflatable, rounded blob) of blue translucent material set in the sunlit grass-and-sky scene or on a white surface beside it; no people, no branded products
q-ml-subject.impact: which materials and forms appear, whether a white receiving surface is in frame, lens choice

q-ml-aspect.default: 3:2 landscape for scenes with grass and sky; 4:5 or 1:1 for single-object material studies; 16:9 when the image is a landing-page hero
q-ml-aspect.impact: how much sky and grass surround the object, whether the transmitted shadow fits in frame
q-ml-aspect.resolve: ask the user, or take it from the landing-page layout later

q-ml-photo-or-render.default: photographic realism with physically correct optics ('hyperreal' read as heightened photography), described in camera and light vocabulary; render vocabulary only for a 3D pipeline
q-ml-photo-or-render.impact: which vocabulary the prompt uses (lens and light vs IOR and path tracing) and how stylized the optics may be

q-ml-other-tints.text: Are untinted clear or other-colored translucent materials allowed alongside the blue?
q-ml-other-tints.default: blue-tinted material dominates; water-clear untinted acrylic allowed as a secondary layer; no green, pink or purple plastic (green belongs to the grass)
q-ml-other-tints.impact: material variety and the colors that appear in overlaps

q-pe-time-of-day.text: What time of day and sun position should images use?
q-pe-time-of-day.default: Clear late morning to early afternoon; sun high and behind or three-quarters behind the subject, so the material is lit through and the framed sky stays deep. Blue hour and underwater are tier-4 options only.
q-pe-time-of-day.impact: light direction, sky saturation, shadow color, caustics
q-pe-time-of-day.resolve: ask the user, or decide per image brief

q-pe-environment-required.text: Must every image include the grass-and-sky environment, or may studio, close-up and abstract images use the palette alone?
q-pe-environment-required.default: Scenes with a ground show sky and grass. Studio, close-up or abstract images keep the triad through a white or pale blue-white backdrop (#DDEDFF) that lets the material's own blue read, blue-tinted white bloom, and at least one green accent (grass blades, or green seen through the material).
q-pe-environment-required.impact: composition, subject choice, how the triad is expressed

q-lp-product.text: What is the landing page for: product, audience and the one conversion action?
q-lp-product.default: A consumer tech or app launch page with one primary action ('Get started' or 'Download') and one secondary ('See how it works').
q-lp-product.impact: page order, hero object, showcase, copy, CTA labels

q-lp-content.text: What copy, imagery and proof (quotes, logos, numbers) exist?
q-lp-content.default: Placeholder copy; hero and showcase images generated with the dump's image export; the proof section left out until real proof exists (no invented testimonials).

material_light._about: The thesis 'color exists inside the material, not painted on', made operational. Layers: material -> light -> perceived color -> camera. Top-level opt-* entries are the optical mechanisms; groups: materials, whites, lighting_camera, invariants (must show in every image), bindings (what each adjective attaches to), descriptors (mood words and the cues that earn them), parameters, exemplars (illustrative). Color reads as inside the material when four things show together: tint depth tracking thickness (inv-ml-depth-tint), white highlights over the blue (inv-ml-white-speculars), transmitted light landing as blue spill (inv-ml-light-lands), and a view into the volume (inv-ml-see-into). Optics are physically grounded; phrasing and numbers are proposals.

us-blue-acrylic-vinyl.text: Transparent blue acrylic and vinyl are the signature materials.

never_implies: a uniform tint of equal strength across the whole object
a colored coating on a clear object
opt-thickness-absorption.text: Color inside a tinted clear material comes from absorption along the light's path: the farther light travels through the blue acrylic, the deeper and more saturated the blue, so thick sections, edges seen end-on and stacked overlaps read deep, while thin sheets read pale. Renderers model this with Beer's law (Autodesk Standard Surface transmission_depth: the distance at which white light becomes exactly the tint color); with zero depth the same tint becomes a constant surface tint, which is the painted-on look to avoid.

opt-transmission.text: Clear acrylic and glass pass light straight through with refraction: you see a sharp but bent view of what lies behind, plus surface reflections. An interior scattering coefficient turns that view milky. A thin sheet such as vinyl film behaves as thin-walled: tinted, with no refraction offset, while a thick acrylic block bends and offsets what is behind it.

opt-subsurface.text: Subsurface scattering: light enters the material, diffuses under the surface and exits at a different point, so the body glows softly from within instead of giving a sharp view through it. This is the frosted, semi-translucent end of the range (the iMac G3 got it from light-scattering particles in the plastic). A little of it makes blue plastic look lit from inside; too much turns it opaque.

opt-caustics.text: Caustics: curved clear or tinted objects bend light into bright patches and bright-edged lines on nearby surfaces (a drinking glass throws a curved bright region inside its own shadow; waves cast rippling caustics). Through tinted acrylic the focused light carries the tint, pooling blue light on the white surface beside the object; this is the physical way color spills onto adjacent whites.

opt-edge-glow.text: Edges glow in two different ways; say which one. Polished cut edges of an acrylic slab or sheet glow deep, saturated blue: light entering the faces is trapped by total internal reflection, travels the long way through the material and exits at the edge, so the edge reads as a luminous line of the most saturated blue in the object. Tapered thin rims and lips, where a rounded form thins out, glow pale and nearly white-blue: light crosses little material there and the rim also catches a bright reflection. Neither is an outline; both come from the light path.

never_implies: an overlap lighter than its layers
opt-overlap-deepening.text: Where tinted layers overlap, light is filtered by each in turn, so the overlap is deeper and darker than any single layer (transmissions multiply). Two pale blue vinyl sheets make a mid blue where they cross; three make a deep blue. A blue layer over the green grass shifts what is behind toward a darker, cooler teal, never toward a lighter or washed blend. An overlap that looks lighter, or unchanged, reads as a flat alpha layer: the painted-on look.

never_implies: a wet film on the surface
opt-specular-highlights.text: Clear plastic, resin and glass reflect the color of the light and sky, not of their tint, so highlights are white or faintly sky-blue and sit on top, with the blue body visible beneath them. That layering, an uncolored surface reflection over a colored volume, is the clearest visible proof that the color is inside. Curvature sets their shape: tight convex curves compress the sun and sky into small, sharp, intense highlights and thin streaks that follow the form; broad flat faces give large soft reflection sheets that can veil the tint, so keep flat faces angled away from the sky.

opt-fresnel-rim.text: Reflection rises steeply at grazing angles: surfaces seen head-on are mostly see-through, while the sides of a curved form, seen nearly edge-on, turn mirror-like and pick up a bright band of sky and white. Rounded acrylic and inflated vinyl get a bright silhouette sheen around a see-through center. Renderers produce it from a correct IOR; in a photographic prompt, 'bright reflective rim, clear center' asks for it.

never_implies: a blue tint over the whole scene
opt-tinted-shadow.text: A clear blue object's shadow is not grey: it is a pool of blue filtered light, deepest under the thickest parts, with bright caustic lines or a bright core where the curved body focuses light. On a white or pale surface it reads as luminous blue light lying on the white; on grass it cools the green toward teal under the object only. Hard direct sun makes shadow and caustics crisp; soft light blurs them into a faint blue haze. This spill is how the material's color reaches the whites around it.

never_implies: a frosted or sanded finish unless asked for

good: a thick slab of transparent blue acrylic, pale at its thin corners, deep sapphire through its middle, polished edges glowing

mat-cast-acrylic.text: Thick, rigid, water-clear plastic tinted blue through its whole body. As a solid form it refracts strongly (the background bends, magnifies, or flips inside spheres and cylinders), the tint deepens toward its thickest point, polished edges glow saturated blue, and highlights stay crisp and white. Forms that show it best: slabs with polished edges, rounded blocks, spheres, lenses, rods, stacked sheets. A solid sphere or lens is deep at the center and pale toward its rim.

mat-vinyl.text: Thin, flexible, tinted PVC: film, sheet, inflatables, or a translucent record. It behaves thin-walled: almost no refraction offset, an even pale-to-mid blue, and color that deepens only where the film doubles up (folds, seams, creases, overlaps). Its highlights are long, soft-edged and wrinkled, following tension in the film. Hollow inflated vinyl reverses the solid rule: the middle (two thin walls) reads pale and clear, the silhouette (seen tangentially through the wall) reads deep blue with a bright Fresnel sheen. A record held to the light is an even blue disc whose grooves catch fine rings of highlight.

mat-opal-acrylic.text: The semi-translucent end of the range: blue plastic with light-scattering particles inside the body (the iMac G3 method), so it glows evenly from within when backlit and shows only faint internal structure instead of a sharp view through. Keep it partly see-through and keep the thickness gradient; push the scattering too far and it becomes opaque milky plastic. A frosted surface (sandblasted, etched) is a different thing: it scatters at the surface and, overdone, reads as a coating.

mat-resin.text: An optional extension beyond the user's acrylic and vinyl: cast resin can hold what acrylic usually doesn't, such as a tint that fades from deep to clear within one piece, tiny suspended bubbles that catch light, or an object embedded and seen through the blue. Use it when an image needs visible depth inside the material. Keep inclusions sparse so it doesn't read as craft-resin kitsch.

mat-blue-glass.text: A secondary material: behaves like thick acrylic (refraction, depth tint, edge glow) but reads heavier, colder and sharper-edged. Ordinary clear window glass shows green edges from its iron content, which pulls against the blue, so ask for blue-tinted or low-iron glass. Plain 'glass' in a prompt drifts toward broken shards, faceted crystal or a frosted UI panel; name the form and the tint.

wh-bloom.text: The brightest points (the sun, specular cores, sunlit thin edges, spill on white) bleed a soft glow a short distance into their surroundings, tinted pale blue by the sky and the material. It is local: halos around light, not a veil over the frame. Small, cool and close to its source reads as luminous; wide, grey or everywhere reads as a dirty lens or fog.

wh-rolloff.text: Whites approach pure white through a gradient of pale blue instead of jumping to a flat clipped plateau: a sunlit white wall runs from blue-white to nearly white, a highlight has a hot core with a pale blue falloff. Near-clipping is welcome; pure clipping is reserved for the sun, specular cores and small light-struck areas. Gradient inside the whites is what separates overexposed on purpose from a lost exposure.

wh-blue-source.text: Give the blue in the whites a physical cause so it stays local and believable: (1) open skylight from the saturated blue sky fills shaded and side-facing white surfaces with blue; (2) light transmitted through the blue material spills onto nearby whites; (3) bloom carries the material's tint into the highlight halos. Whites in full sun and far from the material can sit closest to neutral. This keeps the grass electric green instead of washing the whole frame in a global blue grade.

on_style: midtones keep full saturation: deep blue in thick material, electric green in the grass
whites carry a visible gradient and a blue cast
pure white limited to the sun and highlight cores
shadows are colored and transparent, not lifted grey
bloom is local to bright points
off_style: whole frame lifted and low in contrast
large flat white regions with no gradient
sky clipped to white or cyan, with banding
grey haze over everything from heavy diffusion
wh-luminous-vs-blown.text: Brightness goes into the whites and highlights while the colors beneath keep their saturation; if the blue body or the green grass desaturates, or the whites are flat plateaus, the image reads as overexposed by mistake.

good: the sun three-quarters behind the object, its blue shadow falling toward the camera

lt-ml-backlight.text: The default light: the sun, or one hard key, behind or three-quarters behind the object, so its light passes through the material toward the camera. The body glows, edges and thin rims light up, Fresnel rims brighten, and the tinted shadow falls toward the camera where it can be seen. Front light hides all of this and makes clear plastic look grey and flat.

lt-ml-hard-sun.text: Use a small, hard source: direct sun under a clear sky. Only a hard source draws crisp caustics, sharp-edged blue shadows and tight white highlights; overcast light or big softboxes smear them into a faint haze and make clear plastic dull. The clear blue sky is at the same time a huge soft blue fill, which is what tints shaded whites blue. Outdoors that pair is the whole recipe; in a studio, one hard key behind the object plus a blue-tinted fill.

lt-ml-white-receiver.text: Put a white or pale surface in the transmitted light's path (white ground, plinth, paper sweep, pale wall or stone) so the blue spill and caustics have somewhere to land. Outdoors the grass can receive it, cooling to teal only under the object; add a white element only where the composition allows. With no receiving surface the color stays locked in the object and the spill-onto-whites cue is lost.

cam-ml-lens-angle.text: A short telephoto or macro lens (about 85-100mm full-frame equivalent) close to the object, at a low angle so the object is framed against the saturated sky and the sky is what is seen through it. A moderate aperture (about f/5.6-f/11) keeps the whole object sharp, edges and highlights included, while the far background softens: bokeh belongs to the background and the grass, never to the material.

cam-ml-diffusion.text: A weak diffusion (mist) filter or gentle bloom in post gives the cool halo around highlights. Keep it light, around 1/8 to 1/4 strength: strong diffusion lifts the shadows, greys the colors and softens the material's edges, which is exactly what reads as a failed exposure. Prefer bloom limited to the highlights over a global soft glow.

rv-ml-render-vocab.text: For a 3D pipeline: refraction at IOR about 1.49 (acrylic), volumetric absorption via transmission depth for depth-dependent tint, thin-walled transmission for vinyl film, subsurface scattering for opal plastic, path-traced caustics for colored light on the ground. For a photographic look, describe the visible results instead of stacking render jargon.

inv-ml-depth-tint.invariant: Every translucent blue object shows at least two clearly different depths of the same blue: pale where light crosses little material, deep where it crosses a lot (thick sections, edges seen end-on, overlaps). The gradient follows the form: solid bodies are deepest through their thickest part, hollow shells (inflatables, bubbles) deepest along their silhouette.
inv-ml-depth-tint.variable: object form and scale, thickness range, number of layers, which material (acrylic, vinyl, resin, glass), the exact blue hue
inv-ml-depth-tint.detect: sample the tint at the thinnest and thickest visible parts of each object: lightness and saturation differ clearly (see p-ml-depth-contrast); every overlap is darker than either layer alone
inv-ml-depth-tint.anchor: colors should feel like they exist inside the material
inv-ml-depth-tint.text: The central rule made visible: the blue's depth tracks how far light travels through the material. Thin reads pale; thick, edge-on and overlapped read deep. A uniform blue across an object is the painted-on look, whatever the prompt says.

inv-ml-light-lands.invariant: The light that passed through the material visibly lands somewhere in the frame: a blue-tinted shadow, a caustic pool, or blue spill on an adjacent white or pale surface.
inv-ml-light-lands.variable: which of the three, its strength and sharpness, the receiving surface (white ground, plinth, wall, grass), light direction
inv-ml-light-lands.scope: every image showing the material in direct light
inv-ml-light-lands.detect: each blue object's shadow or nearby white surface contains blue light; no neutral grey shadow under a clear blue object
inv-ml-light-lands.text: Color inside the material is proven again where its light ends up: blue light lying on white, blue shadows with bright caustic cores. A clear blue object with a grey shadow reads as painted.

inv-ml-white-speculars.invariant: Highlights on the material are white or pale sky-blue, sit on its surface and follow its curvature, with the blue body visible beneath them.
inv-ml-white-speculars.variable: number, size and sharpness of highlights (set by light-source size and form curvature)
inv-ml-white-speculars.detect: highlight cores are near-neutral and brighter than any blue in the body; no saturated-blue or metallic highlights
inv-ml-white-speculars.text: The surface carries only uncolored reflections; the color sits underneath. White highlight over blue body is the fastest visual test for color inside versus color on top.

inv-ml-see-into.term: a volume you can see into
inv-ml-see-into.invariant: The material reads as a volume you can see into: through clear parts the background is visible and bent by refraction; in opal parts an inner glow and faint inner structure show.
inv-ml-see-into.variable: clarity from water-clear to opal; what is seen through it (sky, grass, white surface, internal structure)
inv-ml-see-into.detect: something behind or inside each object is visible, offset or magnified in thick clear parts
inv-ml-see-into.text: Transparency must show as depth, not as faintness: the viewer looks into the blue and sees something there.

inv-ml-luminous-whites.term: luminous whites that keep the color
inv-ml-luminous-whites.invariant: Whites are high-key and bloom with a cool blue cast but keep a gradient, while the saturated colors (deep blue in thick material, electric green grass, saturated sky) keep their saturation; pure clipping only at the sun and highlight cores.
inv-ml-luminous-whites.variable: overall key, bloom amount and radius, which surfaces go near-white, how much blue the whites carry
inv-ml-luminous-whites.detect: clipped area is small and confined to light sources and highlight cores (see p-ml-clip); deep-blue and grass regions stay saturated; white areas show a pale-blue gradient, not a flat plateau
inv-ml-luminous-whites.text: 'Overexposed' made safe: the brightness goes into the whites and highlights, never into the colors.

modifies: smooth surfaces of the acrylic, vinyl, resin and glass
the white specular highlights on them
b-ml-glossy.text: 'Glossy' (shiny, glassy, polished) means a dry, hard, clean surface reflection with white highlights over color that lives underneath; never wet, oily, lacquered or chrome.

never_implies: a light source inside the object
b-ml-luminous.text: 'Luminous' and 'glowing' mean daylight passing through and out of the material (edges, inner scattering, bloom, spill); the object has no light of its own.

modifies: the sky right around the sun
b-ml-overexposed.text: 'Overexposed' attaches to the whites and highlights only; the blue material, the grass and the sky stay fully saturated.

modifies: shadows and spill near the blue material
never_implies: a global blue or teal color grade
b-ml-blue-tinted.text: 'Blue-tinted' attaches to whites, halos, shadows and spill near the material, each with a physical cause (skylight, transmitted spill, bloom); a global blue grade would turn the electric green grass teal.

modifies: the material body: transparent = clear with a sharp, refracted view through (acrylic, glass, clear vinyl); translucent = light passes but diffuses (opal plastic, thin frosted film)
never_implies: lower opacity or an alpha fade
b-ml-transparent.text: Transparent gives a sharp, bent view through the body; translucent glows with a softened view. Neither means faint: the material stays present through its tint, edges and highlights.

b-ml-chromatic.text: 'Chromatic' means strong color carried by light through the material, not rainbow, iridescent or holographic surface effects (which undo the color-inside rule) or lens aberration.

cues: the camera-facing side glows when the sun is behind the object
edge glow
blue spill or caustics on adjacent whites
cool bloom at the brightest points
d-ml-luminous.caveat: an impression produced by visible light transmission; the word alone adds little, so put the cues in the prompt
d-ml-luminous.text: 'Luminous' is earned when light visibly passes through the material; write the cues, since the word alone yields generic brightness or an emissive glow.

cues: high-key whites with soft blue bloom
pale thin-sheet and thin-rim tints
forms that hold light rather than block it
colored transparent shadows instead of dark ones
d-ml-ethereal.caveat: an impression, not a property; in prompts 'ethereal' and 'dreamy' pull toward fog, haze, soft focus, pastel washes and fantasy imagery, so use the cues and keep the material crisp
never_implies: soft focus over the whole image
angels, fairies or fantasy light rays
d-ml-ethereal.text: 'Ethereal' here means objects that hold light instead of blocking it, with the material sharp and the sky clear.

cues: an opal or resin body evenly brighter than its surroundings in backlight
soft internal scattering with faint internal structure
glow strongest in thin parts and edges facing the light
d-ml-glow-within.caveat: describes scattered daylight, not an internal lamp; with no backlight the effect disappears
d-ml-glow-within.text: 'Glowing from within' is earned by backlight scattering inside opal plastic or resin; pair it with the light direction ('backlit by the sun') so a model doesn't add a lamp.

cues: a sharp, refracted view of the background through thick parts
crisp white highlights
deep but clean tint without haze
d-ml-crystal-clear.caveat: 'crystal' pulls faceted gemstones and quartz; say 'water-clear' or 'optically clear' when the form is smooth
d-ml-crystal-clear.text: 'Crystal-clear' describes clarity, not form and not lack of color: the body stays blue.

cues: rounded, swollen forms
soft inner scattering with smooth highlight streaks
tint deepening toward a thick center
d-ml-jelly.caveat: Aero writers use it for glossy translucent UI; in image prompts it pulls toward food jelly, gummy candy and slime, so apply it to the look of the surface and body only
d-ml-jelly.text: 'Jelly-like' describes the optics of a rounded translucent body, never an edible or wobbling substance.

p-ml-ior.status: typical handbook values, not fetched in this build; for renderers
p-ml-ior.text: Acrylic about 1.49, glass 1.52, PVC 1.54, epoxy 1.55: close enough that the materials are told apart by form, thickness and surface, not by how much they bend light.

p-ml-transmission-depth.text: In a renderer, set transmission depth (the distance at which white light becomes exactly the tint color) to about half to one times the object's thickest dimension: thin parts stay pale and the thickest part reaches the full tint. Much larger flattens everything pale; much smaller turns the object dark and near-opaque.

p-ml-depth-contrast.unit: minimum CIELAB L* difference between thinnest and thickest visible part of one object
p-ml-depth-contrast.status: proposed threshold for checks, not measured
p-ml-depth-contrast.text: Within one blue object, the thickest or overlapped area should be at least about 25 L* points darker than the thinnest area, and more saturated. Less than that reads as a uniform painted tint.

p-ml-clip.unit: % of frame area at pure white
p-ml-clip.text: Keep fully clipped pixels to roughly 1-10% of the frame, around 5%, and only at the sun, specular cores and small light-struck areas. Large near-white regions are welcome as long as they keep a pale-blue gradient.

p-ml-bloom.unit: % of image width, applied only to highlights already near clipping
p-ml-bloom.text: Bloom spreads about 0.5-2% of the image width from highlights that are already near clipping, tinted pale blue. A radius beyond a few percent, or a threshold low enough to catch midtones, becomes the global haze that reads as a dirty lens.

ex-ml-slab.text: A thick slab of transparent blue acrylic standing on a white plinth, backlit by a high sun under a deep blue sky: pale clear blue at its thin corners, deep sapphire through its center, polished edges glowing a saturated bright blue, crisp white highlights along the top edge, and a sharp blue shadow with bright caustic lines lying on the white surface in front of it.

ex-ml-vinyl-layers.text: Three sheets of translucent blue vinyl film hung in overlapping layers against the sky: each single sheet a pale airy blue, deeper where two overlap, deepest where all three cross, soft wrinkled white highlights along the folds, the sun through them throwing layered blue shadows onto a white wall.

ex-ml-inflatable.text: A translucent blue inflatable vinyl ring resting on electric-green grass in hard midday sun: each tube pale and see-through across its middle and deep blue along its outline, a bright reflective rim on its curves, a blue shadow with a bright caustic crescent cooling the grass to teal only beneath it, whites bright and blooming while the grass stays fully saturated.

ex-ml-opal.text: A rounded, swollen form of semi-translucent blue plastic, softly glowing from within as the sun shines through it from behind, faint internal ribs visible through the body, a tight white highlight streak following its curve, cool blue-white bloom around the brightest point, high-key exposure with whites near clipping and the blue still deep in its thickest part.

good: a thick slab of transparent blue acrylic, pale at the thin edges and deep through the middle
transparent blue acrylic glowing as the sun shines through it from behind
polished blue-tinted glass with crisp white highlights
high-key exposure: blooming blue-white highlights, the blue still deep and saturated
pale glowing thin edges and soft blue shadows under a clear sky

ex-ml-rewrites.text: Weak phrases and their rewrites, paired by position: name the material and its thickness gradient, give glow a light direction, put 'overexposed' on the whites only, turn haze into visible light cues.

palette_environment._about: Perceived color, environment, composition and mood for images, and the color basis the landing_page tokens should derive from. Hex values are proposed, not measured: no reference image was supplied, so treat them as starting points to tune by eye. Hues are HSL/HSV degrees; saturation and value are HSV percentages. Layers: roles and relationships = perceived color; environment = sky, clouds, grass, sunlight; composition = frame layout; mood = feeling, each word tied to visible cues; signals = what a checker can measure. The optics behind these colors live in material_light (opt-*, inv-ml-*); this section gives them hue, value and area. The variant_pool group is tier 4 and opt-in: sample at most one, never apply it by default.

us-blue-tinted-whites.text: Whites are overexposed and tinted blue.

us-grass-sky.term: hyperreal electric green grass under a saturated blue sky
us-grass-sky.anchor: hyperreal electric green grass under a saturated blue sky
us-grass-sky.text: Hyperreal electric-green grass under a saturated blue sky.

pal-sky-field.text: Sky blue is a smooth vertical gradient of light, not a flat fill: deep saturated blue #1F64D4 at the top of the frame, #5E98E4 through the middle, clear light blue #9DCBF4 at the horizon. Hue stays between about 205° and 220° from top to bottom; only lightness and saturation change.

never_implies: one flat swatch for the whole object
purple or violet in the deepest parts
pal-material-blue.text: The blue of the acrylic and vinyl is a ramp set by how far light travels through it, not one swatch: thin vinyl film #B9E0FF, mid-thickness body #2E8BF0, thick cores and stacked overlaps #0A43B0. Polished cut edges glow the most saturated, brightest blue in the object, about #1E6BFF; thin tapered rims go pale blue-white (pal-white-ramp); caustic light pools as #8FC8FF. Deeper means darker and more saturated while staying blue (hue about 205-228°): never aqua at the edges, never violet in the core.

pal-white-ramp.rule: blue channel at or above red in whites: about +8 to +40 levels (8-bit) in blooms and near the material, more in shade; whites in full sun far from the material may come close to neutral, never warm
never_implies: a blue grade over the whole frame
pal-white-ramp.text: Whites are blue-tinted light in three steps: near-clipped cores #F6FAFF, bloom halos and lit white surfaces #DDEDFF, cloud undersides and shadows on white #B3CBEA. Pure #FFFFFF is kept to the sun and specular cores (budget in p-ml-clip). Blue sits above red in the whites, most in shade and near the material; a white in full sun far from the material may come close to neutral but never warm.

pal-grass-ramp.min_saturation: HSV S at least 60% in lit tips and blade bodies
pal-grass-ramp.text: Grass green is a three-step ramp, never one flat green: sunlit, backlit blade tips #A8F03A (yellow-green), blade bodies #3DCB2A, shaded bases #13702A (deep green, not black). Hue stays between about 80° and 140°; below that it turns olive or straw, above it mint or teal and starts to merge with the blue.

p-pe-proportions.text: Default share of the frame: blue (sky plus material) 45-65%, green (grass) 15-35%, white (clouds, bloom, highlights) 5-15%, other accents 0-5%. White is always the smallest field and the brightest. A macro grass shot may swap the blue and green shares; all three roles stay present.

p-pe-seen-through.method: multiply the layer colors channel by channel (sRGB multiply as a quick approximation); a denser blue dye goes darker and cooler
p-pe-seen-through.status: computed from the proposed hexes, not measured
p-pe-seen-through.text: To get the color of something seen through the blue material, multiply, don't average: grass #3DCB2A behind #2E8BF0 acrylic becomes a dark, cooler green of about #0B6F28, and darker still with a denser dye or another layer. The pale mint #36AB8D a 50% opacity overlay gives for the same pair is the painted-on look. The same rule sets web blends (multiply, not opacity).

rel-pe-blue-on-blue.text: A blue object in front of a blue sky separates by value and edges, not by changing its hue: a thick core darker than the sky behind it, glowing cut edges, pale blue-white rims, and clouds or the horizon visibly bent and offset by refraction through the body. Let part of the body cross a cloud, a white surface or the grass so its blue reads as its own, not borrowed from the sky. Never shift the object toward purple, aqua or gray to make it stand out.

never_implies: a blue color filter over the whole frame
rel-pe-colored-darks.text: The scene is high-key, and its darkest values are colored: deep blue thick cores (#0A43B0) and deep green grass bases (#13702A). Shadows on white are pale blue (#B3CBEA), shadows under the material are blue light. No pure black, no neutral gray, no warm cast anywhere; the grass keeps its own green rather than a blue grade over everything.

rel-pe-hue-gap.text: Blue and green stay clearly apart on the hue wheel: grass 80-140°, sky and material 205-228°, nothing in between as a field. No teal, aqua or turquoise band where the grass meets the sky, no teal-tinted grass, no green-tinted acrylic; the only blue-green in the frame is grass seen through the material or lying in its blue shadow. The blue never passes about 230° toward violet.

rel-pe-light-borne.text: The environment follows the same rule as the material: grass blades are thin and translucent, so where the sun is behind them they glow yellow-green from inside; the sky is itself light; clouds and whites are light. Color everywhere reads as light passing through or coming from something, so the acrylic belongs to the scene instead of sitting on top of it.

env-grass.text: Living, dense, fine-bladed grass, from short lawn to low meadow, fully green with no brown patches, straw, bare soil or bright flowers. Sunlit from the side or behind so many blade tips glow yellow-green with light through them, with deep green between the blades. Blades in the focal plane are crisp one by one; the foreground can fall into soft blur (macro grass is a Frutiger Aero motif). Small natural variation in hue and blade angle keeps it real.

never_implies: a stormy or dark dramatic sky
env-sky.note: where the sky is deepest (about 90° from the sun, where skylight polarization peaks) is common photography knowledge, not a source fetched in this build
env-sky.text: A clean, clear daytime sky, deepest blue toward the top of the frame and lightening smoothly to the horizon, with no haze, smog, gray or banding, like vivid slide-film daylight or a polarizer-filtered sky. A high sun keeps most of the framed sky far from it, where clear-sky blue is deepest; sky right beside the sun goes pale. The sky keeps this saturation even while whites and cloud tops bloom: one straight exposure would bleach it, and holding both is part of what reads hyperreal.

env-clouds.text: A few small clouds, not a cloudscape: fair-weather cumulus or thin high cirrus over about 5-25% of the sky, leaving large open blue. Their sunlit tops are where the environment's overexposed whites bloom (#F6FAFF into #DDEDFF); their shaded sides and undersides are pale blue #B3CBEA, never gray or brown. No storm towers, overcast or sunset-colored clouds.

env-sunlight.text: One clear sun in neutral daylight white (never warm), high in the sky, late morning to early afternoon, placed behind or three-quarters behind the subject as lt-ml-backlight sets out. In the environment that same sun lights grass blades from behind so their tips glow, throws crisp blue-tinted shadows across the lawn, and leaves the open blue sky as the fill for every shadow.

modifies: the grass and the environment's color intensity, clarity and detail
never_implies: surreal or impossible scenery such as floating islands or giant objects
a CGI-plastic or video-game render of the landscape
b-pe-hyperreal.text: 'Hyperreal' binds to how the grass and its surroundings are rendered: more saturated, cleaner and crisper than a straight photo, with the sky held deep while the whites bloom, yet lit by one consistent sun with believable shadows. It never implies surreal or impossible scenery, a CGI-plastic landscape, cartoon shading, HDR halos or oversharpening.

inv-pe-fields-focus.term: simple fields, one focal zone of optical complexity
inv-pe-fields-focus.invariant: large simple color fields (sky, grass, white light) take most of the frame; refraction, caustics, overlapping translucent layers and bloom concentrate in one focal zone on the material
inv-pe-fields-focus.variable: subject, focal-zone position, number of translucent objects (1-3), object scale, horizon height and shape, camera height and lens

good: A thick blue acrylic cube resting in short sunlit grass, camera at blade height, deep blue sky filling the upper two-thirds, a pool of blue caustic light on the blades beside it.
A sheet of translucent blue vinyl hung across an empty meadow with the sun behind it; the hill and clouds seen through the sheet are darker and bluer, the rest of the frame plain sky.
Product shot: a clear blue acrylic speaker on a white plinth on a lawn, low horizon, two small blue-white clouds, the plinth glowing pale blue where light passes through the speaker.
bad: Many glass orbs, bubbles, sparkles and lens flares scattered across the whole frame, so no calm field remains.
The blue object set against dark shaded grass, so no light passes through it and it reads as flat blue paint.

inv-pe-fields-focus.ex_note: illustrative exemplars, not derived from a reference
inv-pe-fields-focus.text: Keep the frame simple and the optics rich in one place: wide, calm fields of sky, grass and white light take most of the image, and all the optical complexity (refraction, caustics, layered translucent overlaps, bloom) gathers in one focal zone on the material. Subject, position, scale, horizon and camera may change; the calm-fields-plus-one-rich-zone structure may not.

inv-pe-backed-by-light.invariant: each translucent body is seen against, or lit through, something bright, and part of it crosses a white or green area so its own tint is legible
inv-pe-backed-by-light.variable: which bright backing (sky, cloud, white surface, sunlit grass); how much of the body overlaps grass; backlight versus three-quarter backlight
inv-pe-backed-by-light.text: Color only looks inside a material when light comes through it, so put every translucent body in front of something bright, usually the sky from a low camera, and let part of it cross a cloud, a white surface or the grass so the blue is visibly its own. Where the body overlaps grass it reads deep and dark, which is correct; never fix that by brightening or fading the object.

p-pe-composition.text: Starting numbers for a scene with ground and sky: horizon about a third of the way up the frame (20-45%), calm low-detail fields at least 40% of the frame, the focal zone of optical complexity no more than about 25%, clouds over 5-25% of the sky, camera from blade height to about 1 m, tilted 5-20° up. Close-ups and macro shots may drop the horizon entirely.

cues: large empty fields of sky and grass
a few small clouds
a smooth sky gradient
one focal object
no motion, wind or crowd
d-pe-serene.caveat: an impression, not a measured response
d-pe-serene.text: 'Serene' is earned by emptiness: wide calm fields, a few small clouds, a smooth sky gradient and a single focal object, with nothing moving. Show those cues; the word alone adds nothing.

cues: high-key clear daylight
a deep blue sky overhead
a camera tilted slightly up
healthy green growth
a man-made translucent object at ease in nature
d-pe-optimistic.caveat: an impression, not a measured response
d-pe-optimistic.text: 'Optimistic' is earned by bright clear daylight, a deep sky overhead, a slight upward view, healthy green growth and a man-made translucent object at ease in nature: the hopeful technology-meets-nature mood the lineage credits to Frutiger Aero, not to Y2K.

cues: a tinted translucent plastic body of the late-1990s kind
an idealized, near-empty pastoral field and deep sky
d-pe-nostalgic-futurism.caveat: nostalgia is the viewer's association with c. 1998-2013 consumer tech, not a visible property
never_implies: retro props such as CRT monitors, old operating-system windows, cursors or logos
film grain, scratches or VHS artifacts
d-pe-nostalgic-futurism.text: 'Nostalgic futurism' is earned only by the pairing itself: a tinted translucent plastic body of the late-1990s kind set in an idealized, near-empty field under a deep sky. It needs no retro props; CRTs, OS windows, cursors, logos, film grain or VHS artifacts turn it into a period costume.

cues: clear air all the way to the horizon
crisp blade detail
faintly blue whites under neutral daylight
no dust, haze, grime or wear
d-pe-fresh.caveat: an impression, not a measured response
d-pe-fresh.text: 'Fresh' and 'clean' are earned by clear air all the way to the horizon, crisp blade detail and faintly blue whites under neutral daylight, with no dust, haze, grime or wear on the material.

d-pe-unearned.caveat: a judgment about prompt wording, not a measured effect
d-pe-unearned.text: In image prompts, 'dreamy', 'whimsical' and 'magical' have no visible cue in this palette and pull models toward pastel haze, pink-purple casts, sparkles or soft-focus blur. Leave them out and describe the cues instead: clear air, a deep sky, light passing through blue acrylic.

sig-pe-blue-dominant.term: blue is the largest hue field

test.spec: hue histogram over pixels with HSV S >= 25%: the 200-230° band is the largest hue group and covers >= 40% of the frame (macro grass shots excepted)

sig-pe-blue-dominant.text: On-style images are mostly blue: sky plus material at roughly 40-70% of the frame, the largest hue group. Macro grass shots are the one allowed exception.

test.spec: pixels with V >= 90% and HSV S <= 15%: mean (B - R) >= +4 in 8-bit; warm hues (20-60°, S >= 20%) <= 3% of the frame outside the subject's own colors

sig-pe-blue-whites.text: Whites carry a measurable blue lean on average, and whites, shadows and sky show no warm cast.

sig-pe-sky-held.term: sky stays saturated while whites bloom

test.spec: upper half of the visible sky: >= 80% of its pixels have HSV S >= 45% and are below clipping, even when cloud tops or highlights clip

sig-pe-sky-held.text: The sky keeps its deep saturated blue even where cloud tops and highlights clip; a pale, hazy or white-washed sky is off-style.

sig-pe-grass-range.term: grass is a saturated green ramp

test.spec: grass pixels: hue 80-140°, mean HSV S >= 60%, V spread >= 40 points between the 5th and 95th percentile; straw or soil pixels (hue 25-60°, S < 50%) <= 2% of the grass area

sig-pe-grass-range.text: The grass is saturated green with a real value range from deep bases to glowing tips, with no olive, straw or soil patches and no flat single green.

test.spec: darkest 2% of pixels: >= 90% have HSV S >= 40% with hue in 80-140° or 205-230°; no pixel below V 8%

sig-pe-colored-darks.text: The darkest parts of the image are deep blue cores and deep green grass bases, not black or neutral gray.

sig-pe-fields-focus.term: calm fields with one detail cluster

test.spec: edge-density map (Sobel magnitude on a 16x16 grid): >= 40% of cells are low-detail, and the top-decile detail cells cluster in one region covering <= 25% of the frame; judge by eye if no tooling

sig-pe-fields-focus.text: Most of the frame is calm, low-detail field, and the high-detail optics cluster in one zone rather than spreading everywhere.

var-pe-blue-hour.pool: tier-4 alternative; sample at most one; never a default
never_implies: a sunset orange or pink band
a light source inside the material
var-pe-blue-hour.text: Optional variant, just after sunset: the sky deepens from cobalt #142C78 overhead to clear azure #4F8FE0 at the horizon, with no orange or pink band. One cool lamp or the last bright sky behind the translucent material makes it the brightest thing in the frame, its cut edges glowing #1E6BFF with blue-white bloom #DDEDFF around it. The grass drops to deep green #0E5E2A and turns electric #5FE04A only where the transmitted blue-white light spills onto it. The triad stays; only the balance of light shifts to the material.

var-pe-shallow-water.pool: tier-4 alternative; sample at most one; never a default
var-pe-shallow-water.text: Optional variant, shallow sunlit water seen from below: the water surface replaces the sky as a bright blue-white ceiling #D6F2FF with a sharp circle of sunlight overhead; the water itself is the blue medium, #0F7ED8 near the surface deepening to #0A4FB0; electric-green seagrass or algae #3FD24A replaces the lawn, crossed by a moving net of near-white caustic lines. Keep it blue, not tropical turquoise, and never murky green-brown or deep-sea black.

lineage._about: Named movements and artifacts the aesthetic draws on, each with what it contributes and what it does not. Influences are context, not constraints: the user's own words (core, material_light, palette_environment) outrank them. Borrow the relationship, never the artwork, logo, product silhouette or UI chrome. The contributes/not split is the builder's reading of the cited sources; the dates and facts are from the sources.

us-aero-y2k.text: The vibe draws on Frutiger Aero and Y2K translucency.

inf-frutiger-aero.name: Frutiger Aero
inf-frutiger-aero.period: c. 2004-2013 (CARI: approximately 2005-2013); named retrospectively by Sofi Lee (now Sofi Xian) of the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute, from the Frutiger typeface plus Windows Aero
contributes: blue skies and grass as the default environment
glossy, reflective surfaces and glassy/transparent materials
bokeh, lens flares and aurorae as light motifs
macro photographs of grass
technology shown in harmony with nature
a hopeful, optimistic mood that commentators contrast with Y2K
humanist sans-serif type lineage (Frutiger, Segoe UI)
not: not the Frutiger typeface itself: Wikipedia notes Frutiger was never used in a major UI associated with the style
not flat design, which replaced it in the early 2010s, nor the transitional 'Frutiger Metro' of Windows 8
not a source for 'color inside the material': its gloss is mostly surface highlight and reflection, so it supplies sky, grass and sheen, not volumetric tint
not a license to reuse Windows, Vista, Wii or phone UI assets
inf-frutiger-aero.text: Frutiger Aero (c. 2004-2013): the glossy consumer-tech look of Windows Vista/7, the Wii and early smartphones, named retrospectively by the Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute. It contributes blue skies, grass, bokeh, lens flares and glassy transparent materials in an optimistic technology-meets-nature mood. It does not supply the color-inside-the-material rule; its gloss is mostly surface highlight.

inf-y2k-translucency.name: Y2K translucent tech
inf-y2k-translucency.period: late 1990s to early 2000s; preceded Frutiger Aero
contributes: consumer electronics with translucent casings in vibrant colors, or clear accents
blobject forms: soft, rounded, swollen bodies (the iMac G3 is the textbook case)
see-through housings that let you glimpse internal structure
not: not chromecore: the metallic, mirror-chrome and reflective-clothing branch of Y2K is opaque surface shine, the opposite of color inside the material
not glitter-in-plastic, which sources note sometimes appeared but reads as surface sparkle
not the Y2K software bug
not the source of the optimistic mood: commentators credit that hopefulness to Frutiger Aero, not Y2K
inf-y2k-translucency.text: Y2K translucent tech (late 1990s to early 2000s): computers and consoles made entirely of translucent casing in vibrant colors, or with clear accents, in rounded blobject forms. It contributes the tinted see-through plastic body. It does not contribute chrome, metallic or reflective-clothing looks (chromecore), glitter, or the hopeful mood, which comes from Frutiger Aero.

inf-imac-g3.name: iMac G3 translucent plastics
inf-imac-g3.period: Bondi Blue, 1998; five colors (blueberry, strawberry, tangerine, grape, lime) from January 1999; widely imitated by rival computers and appliances
contributes: a translucent colored plastic body where the color is the material, not a coating
translucency made by mixing light-scattering particles into the plastic instead of texturing the surface: a direct precedent for color inside the material
Bondi Blue, a greenish blue taken from a piece of beach glass
faintly visible internal structure behind a tinted shell
not: not the iMac silhouette, handle, Apple logo or any recognizable Apple product to recreate
not the full fruit range: only the blue end (blueberry, Bondi) serves this aesthetic
not a milky, opaque plastic: the particles diffuse light but the body stays partly see-through
inf-imac-g3.text: iMac G3 (1998, Bondi Blue; 1999 fruit colors): a teardrop translucent plastic case whose translucency came from light-scattering particles mixed into the plastic rather than surface texture. It contributes a tinted body you can partly see into, with color living in the material. It does not license the Apple silhouette, logo or product shape.

inf-aero-glass.name: Windows Aero glass
inf-aero-glass.period: Windows Vista (2006) and Windows 7 (2009); the Glass theme was replaced by a flat theme before Windows 8 (2012), where blur-behind no longer renders
contributes: window frames as translucent, blurred glass sheets over the desktop
the 'sheet of glass' idea: blur applied to a whole window surface with no visible border
a layer that reads as a physical pane because it blurs what lies behind it
not: not a flat alpha overlay: Aero glass blurs the content behind it rather than merely fading it
not Windows title bars, the Start orb, Segoe UI or any Microsoft chrome as an asset
not the dump's saturated blue body: Aero glass is a thin, pale pane, while the user's acrylic is thick and deeply tinted
inf-aero-glass.text: Windows Aero glass (Vista 2006, Windows 7 2009): Microsoft's design language emphasizing animation, glass and translucency, whose signature effect is a translucent, blurred window frame that can extend across a whole window as a sheet of glass. It contributes the blurred-pane-over-a-scene relationship. It does not contribute deep tinted color or any Windows UI asset.

inf-bliss.name: Bliss (Windows XP default wallpaper)
inf-bliss.period: photograph by Charles O'Rear; default wallpaper of Windows XP (early 2000s, between Y2K and Frutiger Aero); Microsoft obtained full rights in 2000
contributes: the green rolling hill / saturated blue sky / white cirrus cloud triad as the environmental archetype
saturation that came from film (Fujifilm Velvia) and daylight, not digital painting: O'Rear says it was not manipulated
a near-empty composition: one hill, sky, a few clouds, distant mountains
not: not the photograph itself or a recognizable recreation of its hill line and cloud layout: it is a rights-held image
not formally part of Frutiger Aero: Wikipedia lists it only under 'See also'
not a translucency source: it contains no translucent material, only the environment
inf-bliss.text: Bliss (Charles O'Rear's photograph, Windows XP default wallpaper): a lush green rolling hill with cirrus clouds in a daytime sky, shot on Velvia film that saturated greens and blues, not digitally manipulated. It contributes the hyperreal green-hill-under-blue-sky archetype with saturation from film and light. It does not contribute translucency, and the photo itself must not be recreated.

inf-translucent-vinyl.name: translucent colored vinyl records
inf-translucent-vinyl.period: since the mid-1940s: RCA Victor transparent red vinylite 78s (1945), the first 45 rpm record (1948) pressed in yellow translucent vinyl, a translucent blue vinyl stereo LP (1957)
contributes: a PVC body you can hold up to the light, with the color in the disc itself
a precedent for translucent blue vinyl specifically, decades before Y2K
not: not specific to Y2K or Frutiger Aero: the sources tie it to record history, not either movement
not opaque, marbled or picture-disc pressings, which hide the see-through quality
inf-translucent-vinyl.text: Translucent colored vinyl: PVC records pressed in transparent and translucent colors since the 1940s, including translucent blue. It contributes the vinyl half of the user's 'acrylic and vinyl' material pair, a tinted disc or sheet you see light through. It is an older material tradition, not a Y2K or Frutiger Aero artifact.

inf-liquid-glass.name: Apple Liquid Glass
inf-liquid-glass.period: announced June 9, 2025; Wikipedia reports TechRadar's view that it was likely influenced by Frutiger Aero
contributes: current UI vocabulary for a translucent material that reflects and refracts its surroundings
material color informed by the content around it, adapting between light and dark
specular highlights that respond to movement
not: not Apple's controls, icons or chrome to copy
not the dump's deep blue body: Liquid Glass takes its color from surrounding content rather than carrying a strong tint of its own
inf-liquid-glass.text: Apple Liquid Glass (2025): a contemporary translucent UI material that reflects and refracts its surroundings and takes its color from nearby content, reportedly influenced by Frutiger Aero. It is a modern web/UI analog for refractive panels with live highlights. It does not supply the saturated tint, which in this aesthetic lives inside the material itself.

m-bliss-field.term: Bliss relationship: saturated field under saturated sky
m-bliss-field.motif: Bliss: one green rolling hill under a deep blue sky with cirrus clouds
