m-bliss-field.relationship: a single, simple, saturated grass field meeting a saturated sky in high-key daylight, near-empty composition, with saturation earned from light and film-like color response rather than paint
m-bliss-field.translation: build original landscapes with your own horizon line, hill shape and cloud pattern; never a recognizable recreation of the photograph; describe it as vivid film-like daylight color, not as 'Windows XP wallpaper'
m-bliss-field.text: Borrow Bliss's relationship, not the photo: one simple saturated grass field meeting a saturated blue sky in bright daylight, almost empty, its color coming from light and film-like response. Use an original horizon, hill shape and cloud pattern; never name or recreate the wallpaper.

m-aero-glass-pane.term: Aero glass relationship: a pane that blurs what is behind it
m-aero-glass-pane.motif: Windows Vista/7 Aero glass window frames
m-aero-glass-pane.relationship: a translucent pane that blurs whatever lies behind it, so the layer reads as a physical sheet in front of a scene; can extend across a whole surface as a sheet of glass
m-aero-glass-pane.translation: on a page: backdrop blur behind panels that also carry their own internal tint and bright edges, over a real scene (sky, grass) rather than an empty gradient; never Windows title bars, orbs, Segoe UI or Microsoft chrome
m-aero-glass-pane.text: Borrow Aero glass's relationship, not its chrome: a pane that blurs the scene behind it so it reads as a physical sheet. In this aesthetic the pane is also tinted from within and glows at its edges; never reuse Windows UI elements.

m-imac-tinted-body.term: iMac G3 relationship: color made inside the plastic
m-imac-tinted-body.motif: iMac G3 Bondi Blue translucent case
m-imac-tinted-body.relationship: a colored plastic body you can partly see into, whose color and glow come from particles inside the plastic rather than surface treatment, with internal structure faintly visible
m-imac-tinted-body.translation: show translucent blue bodies with depth, soft internal glow and faint internal structure; no iMac silhouette, handle, Apple mark or recognizable product shape
m-imac-tinted-body.text: Borrow the iMac G3's relationship, not its shape: a blue plastic body you can partly see into, its color and glow made inside the material, with faint internal structure showing. No Apple silhouette, handle or logo.

kw-frutiger-aero.text: Primary search and tag term for the look; Dazed reported the #frutigeraero TikTok hashtag above 28M views in February 2023 and a fast-growing r/FrutigerAero. Candidate vocabulary: no other measured volume.

kw-web20-gloss.text: Alternate names for Frutiger Aero: 'Web 2.0 Gloss' (Wikipedia) and 'Aero', 'Aqua', 'Web 2.0' (CARI). 'Aqua' and 'Aero' collide with Apple's and Microsoft's UI names, so pair them with 'aesthetic' when searching. Candidate vocabulary.

kw-y2k-translucent.text: Search phrases for the Y2K half: 'translucent casing', 'clear accents', 'blobject', 'Y2K clear plastic' electronics. Candidate vocabulary; exclude 'chromecore' and 'cybercore', which name the metallic branch.

kw-aero-descriptors.text: Descriptor words writers and archivists use for the look: glossy, glassy, translucent, jelly-like, glowing, bubbly, bokeh, lens flare, aurora, macro grass, skeuomorphic, humanist sans-serif, inner glow. Candidate vocabulary; most describe surface gloss, so pair them with the material_light terms for color inside the material.

landing_page._about: Translates the aesthetic to a web landing page (J3) and gives page-side signals for checks (J4). Layers: scene (sky, horizon bloom and grass behind everything) / material (translucent panels, nav, CTAs, hero object) / light (edge highlights, inner glow, colored spill, bloom) / type / motion. Color tokens are taken from palette_environment's ramps (pal-sky-field, pal-white-ramp, pal-material-blue, pal-grass-ramp) so the page matches the generated imagery; the only additions are the page-specific plate white, the CTA body midpoint, the ink and grass-ink text colors. Every hex, alpha, px and ms value is a proposed, illustrative token, not a measurement. Contrast ratios were computed with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula against the stated backdrops; recompute them after changing any token. Borrow relationships from the lineage, never Windows, Apple or other OS chrome.

inv-lp-color-inside.term: color inside the material, on the page
inv-lp-color-inside.anchor: colors should feel like they exist inside the material
inv-lp-color-inside.invariant: Every translucent surface on the page (panels, nav, CTAs, hero object) carries its own blue tint whose density varies with apparent thickness: paler on the thin face, deeper at the rim and where layers overlap. One shared light gives each surface a bright entry edge and a glowing exit edge, and tinted light spills onto whatever lies beneath.
inv-lp-color-inside.variable: which elements are translucent, corner radius, tint strength per panel, live blur or none, number of panels, layout and content
inv-lp-color-inside.text: On the web, color lives inside the material when each surface is built as a tinted slab, not a colored or frosted fill. Each one gets a blue tint that deepens toward rims and overlaps, a bright top edge and a glowing bottom edge from one light, and blue light spilling onto the surface below. A single flat fill, a uniform white frost or a grey drop shadow puts the color on the surface instead.

good: Feature card on page white: face #E2EFFE at the top deepening to #C7E0FC along the lower rim, a 1px near-white line on the top edge, a soft blue glow pooled inside the bottom edge, blue haze pooling 18px below the card.

Primary pill CTA: body #1457D8 darkening to #0A43B0 at its base, a curved white reflection across the top third, pale blue light rising from the bottom rim, white label in the clear band between them.
Hero object: a thick rounded acrylic lens standing on the grass, deep blue where it is thick and pale at its thin edge, throwing a bright blue caustic pool onto the grass and the white beside it.
Sticky nav as one long pane of pale acrylic: the sky stays visible and softened through it, a bright hairline on its top edge, a deeper blue hairline on its bottom edge.
bad: Card: rgba(255,255,255,0.2) fill, backdrop-filter: blur(20px), 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.3) border, 0 8px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.25) shadow. Colorless frost with a grey shadow: generic glassmorphism.
Card: solid #2E8BF0 fill, white text (3.5:1), flat 8px radius. The color is paint, with no thickness, edge or glow, and the text fails contrast.
Button: silver-to-white chrome gradient with a mirror sheen. Opaque metallic surface shine (chromecore), not tinted light passing through.

test.spec: shown the page, a reviewer can point to where each translucent surface's blue gets deeper (rim, overlap), where light enters (top edge) and where tinted light lands (spill below); any surface that is one flat fill fails

inv-lp-single-light.term: one light for the whole page
inv-lp-single-light.invariant: All specular highlights sit on the same edges (top, or top-left), all inner glows on the opposite exit edge, all spill falls away from the light, and the hero scene's sun or brightest bloom sits on the light's side.
inv-lp-single-light.variable: light angle within roughly 0-30 degrees of straight down from above; highlight strength per component
inv-lp-single-light.text: Use one light for every surface. Highlights go on the top (or top-left) edges, glow on the bottom inner edges, blue spill below and slightly away from the light, and the hero sun or bloom on the same side. Mixed light directions break the illusion of a physical material faster than any wrong color.

test.spec: for the nav, every card, every CTA and the hero object, name the edge with the brightest highlight; all must agree, and spill must fall on the opposite side

inv-lp-scene-behind.invariant: Live-blurred translucent panels sit over something with structure: sky with clouds, the horizon bloom, grass, the hero object, or another tinted layer.
inv-lp-scene-behind.variable: photographic, rendered or illustrated scene; how much of it each panel covers
inv-lp-scene-behind.text: Translucency needs something behind it to bend. Put blurred panels over the sky, clouds, grass or the hero object. In plain white sections, cards drop live blur and carry the effect with tint depth, edges, glow and spill alone. Never invent random blurred color blobs just to give the glass something to show.

inv-lp-localized.invariant: Large calm fields (sky, blue-tinted white, grass) dominate the page; the full optical treatment (gloss, caustics, bloom, sweep) is concentrated on the hero object and the primary CTAs.
inv-lp-localized.variable: which one or two features get the full treatment; how many cards appear
inv-lp-localized.text: Keep optical complexity local, as the images do. The hero object and primary CTAs get the full treatment: gloss, caustic spill, bloom, the specular sweep. Cards get tint depth, edges and a quiet glow. Body copy, nav links and forms stay calm and flat-lit. Most of the page is large simple fields of sky, blue-tinted white and grass.

test.spec: per viewport: at most one hero object and two CTAs carry gloss plus caustic spill; at most one element runs the specular sweep at a time

never_implies: one identical fill alpha for every panel
deepening by mixing in black or grey
deep tint directly behind body text without a plate
w-lp-tint-thickness.text: Map Beer's-law depth onto layered tints. Give each panel a nominal thickness, thin, medium or thick: acrylic body blue #2E8BF0 at 0.08, 0.16 or 0.28 alpha, deepening toward the lower rim in core blue #0A43B0. The tints are semi-transparent saturated blue, so overlapping panels composite deeper on their own, the way stacked acrylic does: two medium layers over #F6FAFF go from #D6E8FD to #BBD9FB. Stacked white frost does the opposite and washes out: two 0.2 white layers over the mid sky go from #7EADE9 to #98BDED. Use thickness to rank surfaces: featured card or hero panel thick, supporting cards medium, nav thin.

w-lp-edge-light.text: Edges carry the light and prove the thickness: a near-white 1px line on the top edge where light enters, a deeper core-blue 1px line on the bottom rim, a faint blue outline all round. For a lit border, put a transparent border over a border-box gradient that runs white at the top through pale caustic blue to core blue at the bottom, with a padding-box fill. A uniform 1px white border, the frosted-glass default, reads as a flat sticker.

w-lp-inner-glow.text: Inner glow is light that entered and scattered inside: a pale caustic-blue (#8FC8FF) inset glow pooled along the lower inner edge, where light exits, plus a faint ambient inset glow. Keep it blue, never cyan or aqua. A little reads as lit from within; past about 0.6 alpha, or spread evenly over the whole face, the panel goes milky and opaque.

w-lp-light-spill.text: Shadows are colored light, not darkness. Under each translucent object a blurred blue spill pools on the surface below, with a small, faint core-blue contact shadow for grounding. Beside the hero object, add a caustic pool on the white or the grass: an ellipse with a hot white core fading through pale blue to transparent, offset away from the light. Grey or black drop shadows set the object on top of the page; tinted spill shows light passing through it.

w-lp-backdrop.term: backdrop blur as a supporting layer
w-lp-backdrop.text: Blur is the supporting layer, not the effect. Apply backdrop-filter: blur(14px) saturate(1.4) (8-20px) to the nav and at most one or two hero panels over the scene, so the sky and grass behind stay recognizable but softened. Cards in plain sections or scrolling grids skip live blur. Generic glassmorphism makes the blur the whole effect; here the tint, edges and spill carry it, and the page must still look right with blur switched off.

w-lp-bloom-whites.text: Page whites are blue-tinted, from the white ramp: #F6FAFF for the page field, #EAF4FF for text plates, #DDEDFF for bloom halos and alternate section bands, #B3CBEA for shadows and dividers on white. Overexposure lives in bloom, not in the copy: soft radial glows of near-white around the hero sun, along the horizon band and on the hero object's highlights, fading into sky blue. Pure #FFFFFF is reserved for small specular highlights and for text on deep blue. Text never sits inside a bloom core.

p-lp-color-sky.text: The sky stops from pal-sky-field, so the page matches the generated hero image: zenith #1F64D4 (white text 5.5:1), mid #5E98E4 (navy 5.2:1, white 3.0:1, below the large-text minimum), horizon #9DCBF4 (navy 9.0:1).

p-lp-color-whites.text: Blue-tinted whites from pal-white-ramp, plus one derived plate step: page #F6FAFF; plate #EAF4FF at 0.78 alpha or more behind any text over the scene; lit #DDEDFF for bloom halos and alternate bands; shade #B3CBEA for shadows and dividers on white; specular #FFFFFF only for small highlights and for text on deep blue.

p-lp-color-acrylic.text: Acrylic blues from pal-material-blue. Body #2E8BF0 is used only as alpha tints: white text on it is 3.5:1. Edge #1E6BFF is the brightest saturated accent (white 4.6:1, no gloss allowed behind text). Core #0A43B0 is for rims and the deepest parts. Caustic #8FC8FF is for inner glow and light pools. The CTA body runs from #1457D8 (the edge-to-core midpoint) down to #0A43B0: white label 6.2:1 at its lightest, 4.6:1 under a 0.15 white gloss.

p-lp-color-grass.text: Electric grass from pal-grass-ramp: tips #A8F03A, blade body #3DCB2A, shaded base #13702A, plus #06380F as ink for text on green (6.2:1 on the blade body). The bright greens are fields and accents, never text on white (2.1:1); the deep base #13702A can carry text (5.9:1 on page white, white on it 6.2:1).

p-lp-color-ink.text: Navy ink #0A2350 for headings and body (14.6:1 on page white); muted #34507F for secondary text (7.7:1 on page white, 6.8:1 on lit white, never on open sky); white only on deep blue. Ink is a colored dark like the rest of the palette, never pure black, which reads as print laid on top of the light.

p-lp-gradient-sky.text: Hero sky as a vertical gradient ending in horizon bloom where the grass begins, at about 86% of the hero height. With these stops, text zones fall out as follows: white body text only in the top ~14% (sky #3274D9 or deeper); white display text (24px and up) down to about 44%; navy body text from about 37% down through the horizon (4.6:1 rising to 9.0:1); between ~16% and ~35% (#3576DA to #4E8BE0) neither white nor navy reaches 4.5:1. Lay original clouds and the grass field over it as image or illustration; the gradient alone is a fallback, not the scene.

p-lp-face-recipe.shadow_stack: var(--edge-specular), var(--edge-rim), var(--edge-outline), var(--glow-exit), var(--shadow-spill), var(--shadow-contact)
p-lp-face-recipe.text: One panel recipe, top layer first: a top sheen (white 0.55 fading to 0 by 32%), a tint-depth layer (acrylic body blue 0.06 at the top to 0.20 at the bottom), then the #EAF4FF plate at 0.78 when the panel holds text (omit the plate on decorative panels). Shadow stack: edge specular, rim, outline, exit glow, spill, contact. Worst case, over the zenith sky, the bottom of the face is #A0C5F5: navy text 8.6:1, muted text only just 4.5:1, so over deep sky keep muted text in the upper half.

p-lp-gloss-pill.text: Gel-pill CTA fill: a curved white reflection in the top third fading to 0 by 38% of the height, a pale blue exit glow in the bottom 30%, over the #1457D8-to-#0A43B0 body. The label sits in the clear middle band, where gloss is 0.15 alpha or less and the glow has not started: white is 6.2:1 on the body's lightest point, 4.6:1 under 0.15 gloss, 4.2:1 under 0.20 (fails), and 4.2:1 where the glow reaches 0.3. A gloss or glow that reaches the label fails contrast.

p-lp-radius.text: Soft, swollen geometry from the blobject lineage: cards 24px (20-28), large panels 32px, CTAs full pills, icon tiles 16px. Sharp corners and 4-8px radii read as flat UI; the radius is part of what makes a panel read as a molded slab.

qualities: open apertures (c, e, s, a open wide)
proportions drawn from handwriting, not circles
avoid: Frutiger, Myriad or Segoe UI as the signature face: each is tied to a brand or an OS, and Segoe UI reads as Windows chrome
neo-grotesque defaults (Inter, Helvetica, Arial) as the voice: they read as generic SaaS
bubble, chrome or novelty 'Y2K' display fonts
never_implies: gradient-filled, glossy, beveled or glowing text
t-lp-humanist.text: Set the page in a humanist sans: open apertures, slight stroke modulation, handwriting-derived proportions, a calm upright rhythm. That carries Frutiger Aero's friendly, legible type lineage without copying it; never use Frutiger, Myriad or Segoe UI as the signature face. Navy ink (#0A2350), not black; white only on deep blue. No gradient-filled, glossy, beveled or glowing text: the material effects belong to surfaces, and the type stays crisp on top of them.

p-lp-type-candidates.status: candidates; verify license, glyph coverage and metrics before shipping
p-lp-type-candidates.text: Open-license, humanist-leaning candidates; use one family for the whole page: Source Sans 3, Fira Sans or Noto Sans (all on Google Fonts under the SIL Open Font License; confirm before shipping). Choose by x-height and aperture at 16-18px, and load two or three weights (400, 600, 700) as a variable or subset WOFF2. A brand face replaces these if the product has one (q-lp-brand-fonts).

p-lp-type-scale.text: Calm, generous scale: 18px body at 1.6 line height, 24px h3, fluid 32-44px h2 and 44-76px display, display tracking -0.015em, small caps labels +0.04em, line length 60-68ch. Only large text (24px and up, or 18.66px bold) may sit at 3:1 contrast, which is what lets a white display headline sit lower on the sky than white body text.

when.page: single landing page, content not yet known

then: sticky acrylic nav
hero: sky over grass, one acrylic hero object, headline, primary and secondary CTA
three feature cards on page white
showcase: close-up of the product or an acrylic object with caustic light
proof (quotes, logos, numbers) on plates, only if real proof exists
closing CTA band on the bright lower sky or on page white
footer standing on a grass strip, its text on plates or on the deep grass base
g-lp-page-order.text: Default structure, read as one vertical landscape: sky and hero at the top, white content in the middle like the bright air above the horizon, and the page ending on the grass. Nav, hero, three feature cards, showcase, proof, closing CTA band, footer on a grass strip. Replace with the real content plan once the product is known (q-lp-product).

then: one sticky pane: a full-width bar, or a floating pill inset 12-16px from the edges, 60-68px tall
fill #EAF4FF at 0.78 with backdrop blur(14px) saturate(1.4): a thin tint (navy links 10.2:1 even over the zenith)
top specular hairline, bottom rim hairline, faint blue spill below
navy links 15-16px weight 500; one small primary pill on the right
raise the fill to 0.90 once scrolled past the hero so links over busy content keep contrast
no title-bar caption buttons, Start orb, taskbar or OS menu chrome
g-lp-nav.text: The nav is one long pane of thin, pale acrylic: the scene stays visible and softened through it, a bright hairline marks the top edge and a deeper blue hairline the bottom. Navy links, one small primary pill. It gets more opaque after the hero so contrast holds over content. It must never resemble an OS title bar or taskbar.

then: full-bleed original scene: saturated sky (p-lp-gradient-sky) over an electric-green grass field from about 86% down, a few soft original clouds, bloom along the horizon
one hero object in thick blue acrylic or tinted vinyl (an abstract lens, droplet or pill, or the product itself rendered in acrylic), on or just above the grass, deep where thick and pale where thin
a blue caustic pool beside the object on the grass or the white, offset away from the light
headline and subcopy in navy in the bright lower sky above the horizon (5-9:1), or a white display headline high in the zenith; body copy over the upper sky goes on a plate
one primary CTA and one secondary, placed on the lower sky, a plate or the zenith, never in the mid-sky band
wide calm negative space around the object
imagery generated with the dump's image export or rendered; never the Bliss photograph or a recognizable recreation of its hill and clouds
g-lp-hero.text: The hero is the aesthetic in one frame: an original saturated sky over electric-green grass, bloom along the horizon, and one thick blue acrylic object catching the light and pooling blue light on the ground beside it. Because the image-matched sky is light in its lower half, the natural text home is navy type in the luminous band above the horizon, or a white display headline high in the zenith. One primary and one secondary CTA, and most of the frame left as calm open field.

then: face from p-lp-face-recipe; radius 24px; padding 28-32px
on white sections: no live blur; tint depth, edges, glow and spill only
over the scene: live blur only within the viewport budget (perf-lp-backdrop)
rank by thickness: one featured card thick, the rest medium
let one card or the showcase panel overlap another surface so the overlap visibly deepens
icon: a small glossy acrylic glyph or a navy line icon; no emoji or clip-art
navy headings; navy or muted body per a-lp-text-zones
g-lp-card.text: A feature card is a slab of pale blue acrylic: deeper toward its lower rim, lit along its top edge, glowing softly at the bottom, with a blue haze beneath. On white sections it needs no live blur. One featured card is thicker than the rest, and where a card overlaps another surface the overlap reads deeper.

when.backdrop: page white, lit white, plate, or the lower sky and horizon

then: gel pill from p-lp-gloss-pill, height 48-56px, horizontal padding 28px
white label 16-17px weight 600 in the clear middle band
blue spill below (--shadow-spill) and a white specular hairline on the top edge
the pill's edge is 5.9-8.2:1 against page white and 3.6-5.0:1 against the horizon, so it reads clearly as a control
g-lp-cta-on-light.text: On light backdrops the primary CTA is a deep acrylic gel pill: body darkening from #1457D8 to #0A43B0, a curved reflection in the top third, pale blue glow rising from the bottom rim, white label in the clear band between them, blue spill below.

g-lp-cta-on-sky.term: primary CTA on the deep sky

when.backdrop: upper sky (zenith toward the mid stop)

then: switch to the light acrylic pill: opaque #EAF4FF (edge 4.9:1 against the zenith, navy label 13.8:1) or #EAF4FF at 0.85 (edge 4.0:1, label 11.2:1), white top specular, core-blue hairline at the bottom
never a deep blue pill straight on deep sky: #0A43B0 against #1F64D4 is 1.6:1 and #1457D8 is 1.1:1, so the button dissolves
never in the mid-sky band: no pill, light or deep, reaches 3:1 against #5E98E4
g-lp-cta-on-sky.text: On the deep sky a deep blue pill disappears, so the primary CTA flips to light acrylic with a navy label. In the mid-sky band neither version separates from the sky, so CTAs move up to the zenith or down to the bright lower sky. The choice is per backdrop, not per brand color.

then: clear acrylic pill: #EAF4FF at 0.78 with a thin tint, rim outline rgba(10,67,176,0.35), navy label
no gloss reflection and no sweep: the primary owns the gloss
never a ghost text link or a 1px white outline straight on the sky
g-lp-cta-secondary.text: The secondary CTA is a clear, lightly tinted acrylic pill with a navy label and a thin blue rim, quieter than the primary and never a bare outline floating on the sky.

then: one large close-up of the product housing, or an abstract object, in translucent blue acrylic or vinyl, with faint internal structure visible through the tint
set on page white, with a caustic pool and blue spill on the ground plane
copy beside it on page white, not over the object
no iMac silhouette, handle or other recognizable consumer-product shape
g-lp-showcase.text: The showcase is the page's close-up: one object made of tinted acrylic or vinyl, internal structure faintly visible, light pooling blue on the white beside it, with the copy set alongside on clean blue-tinted white.

tokens.band: white at 0.5-0.6 alpha, about 20% of the element's width, angled with the page light

mo-lp-specular-sweep.text: One narrow highlight band crosses the hero object or the primary CTA once after first paint and once per hover, 600-800ms ease-out, angled with the page light. Animate transform on a clipped pseudo-element; never animate background-position over large areas or the blur radius. No looping shimmer. Under reduced motion there is no sweep and the highlight rests at its final position.

mo-lp-states.text: Hover: the light strengthens (exit glow +0.15 alpha, spill +0.10) over 160ms with a 1-2px lift; the glow still stays below the label. Press: the highlight dims, the rim deepens and the lift returns to 0 in 90ms, as if pressing into the acrylic. Focus: the ring from a-lp-focus appears instantly. Reduced motion keeps the light changes and drops the lift.

mo-lp-ambient.text: Optional and quiet: clouds drift on a cycle of 60s or longer, and sky, grass and hero object separate by at most 12px of parallax while scrolling through the hero. Pause when off-screen and under reduced motion. No autoplaying video behind blurred panels: a moving backdrop makes every frame re-blur.

m-lp-aero-light.term: Aero relationship on the page: light through the pane
m-lp-aero-light.motif: Windows Vista/7 Aero glass frames and glossy taskbar buttons
m-lp-aero-light.relationship: light passes through a tinted pane: a bright upper edge where it enters, a glow at the lower edge where it exits, the scene behind visible but softened
m-lp-aero-light.translation: panels, nav and CTAs show light entering at the top and glowing out at the bottom over the page's own sky and grass; never title bars, caption buttons, the Start orb, the taskbar, Aero window frames, Segoe UI as the signature face, or Windows wallpapers
m-lp-aero-light.text: Borrow Aero's light-through-glass relationship, not Windows chrome: each pane shows where light enters (bright top edge) and leaves (glow at the bottom) over a softened scene. Nothing on the page should be recognizable as a Windows window, button, orb, taskbar or wallpaper.

m-lp-gel-button.relationship: a pill whose top carries a curved specular reflection and whose bottom glows with transmitted light, so it reads as a drop of tinted acrylic
m-lp-gel-button.translation: one reflection per pill from the page's shared light, kept above the label; no wet-floor mirror reflections, starburst badges, bevel-and-emboss or glossy text
m-lp-gel-button.text: Borrow the gel button's relationship: a pill that reads as a drop of tinted acrylic, with a curved reflection on top and light glowing out of its base. Keep exactly one reflection, from the page's light, above the label, and leave the period's clip-art behind.

m-lp-liquid-glass.relationship: a refractive layer whose specular highlights respond to movement, so the material feels live
m-lp-liquid-glass.translation: optional pointer- or scroll-reactive highlight on the hero object and primary CTA only; keep this page's own saturated tint (Liquid Glass takes its color from surrounding content); no Apple controls, icons, system type or tab-bar shapes
m-lp-liquid-glass.text: From Liquid Glass, borrow only the live highlight that shifts with pointer or scroll, and only on the hero object and primary CTA. The saturated tint stays this page's own, and nothing should resemble Apple's controls.

never_implies: an opacity drop on a whole component, label included
b-lp-translucent.text: 'Translucent', 'transparent' and 'glass' describe surfaces only: the panels, nav, CTAs and hero object let tinted light and the scene through. They never apply to text or labels, never mean lowering a whole component's opacity, and never mean a colorless white frost.

b-lp-overexposed.text: 'Overexposed' and 'luminous' bind to the light sources: the horizon band, the hero sun, speculars and caustic pools. They never mean washed-out text, pure-white page fields, glare over copy or a low-contrast pastel interface.

b-lp-glossy.text: 'Glossy' binds to the primary CTAs, the hero object and small icon glyphs. It never means glossy or gradient-filled text, gloss on every element, wet-floor reflections, or a chrome or metallic sheen.

a-lp-contrast-pairs.status: computed with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula for these tokens; recompute after any token change
a-lp-contrast-pairs.text: Contrast is measured per backdrop, including the worst case behind each translucent layer. Navy on any plate, white field or the lower sky passes (5.2-14.6:1); white passes on the zenith and the CTA body (5.5-6.2:1) and fails on the mid sky even for large text; electric green fails as text and behind white text, while the deep grass base passes. Automated checkers generally cannot resolve text over images, gradients or backdrop blur and flag it for manual review, so sample screenshot pixels behind every text block at its brightest and darkest point.

test.spec: for every text node, sample the lightest and darkest backdrop pixels inside its box in a screenshot; ratio >= 4.5:1, or >= 3:1 for text 24px and up or 18.66px bold and up

a-lp-text-zones.invariant: Body text sits only where the measured backdrop gives 4.5:1 or better: on plates, on blue-tinted whites, in navy on the lower sky and horizon, or in white high in the zenith.
a-lp-text-zones.variable: plate opacity at or above 0.78; which zone a headline uses
a-lp-text-zones.text: Translucency is for surfaces, never for the text on them. Body text sits on an #EAF4FF plate at 0.78 or more, on the page and lit whites, in navy on the sky from about 37% of the hero height down (sky #518EE1 or lighter), or in white only in the top band of the zenith (sky #3274D9 or deeper). The band in between (#3576DA to #4E8BE0) is under 4.5:1 for both white and navy, so no body text goes there. Muted ink never goes on open sky. No text directly on the bright grass or inside a bloom core.

a-lp-green-text.text: The electric grass greens (#3DCB2A body, #A8F03A tips) are field and accent colors: the body is 2.1:1 as text on white and 2.2:1 behind white text. Text on bright green uses grass ink #06380F (6.2:1) or navy (7.1:1). The deep base #13702A is the one green that can carry text (5.9:1 on page white; white on it 6.2:1). Do not make the primary CTA green by default; if a green CTA is wanted, it takes a dark label.

a-lp-focus.text: Every interactive element gets a visible two-tone focus ring, 2px navy inside 2px white, so at least one tone clears 3:1 against any backdrop in this palette (navy on page white 14.6:1, white on the zenith 5.5:1, navy on the mid sky 5.2:1, navy on grass 7.1:1). Show it on :focus-visible; never remove outlines without this replacement, and never signal focus with a glow alone.

test.spec: tab through the page in a headless browser; every focusable element matches :focus-visible and a before/after screenshot diff around it is non-empty

a-lp-reduced-motion.text: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop the specular sweep, cloud drift and parallax, and remove lifts. Keep instant or short (150ms or less) color and glow changes so state stays visible, and leave highlights static at their resting positions so the page looks finished, not broken.

test.spec: emulate prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (for example Playwright page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion: 'reduce'})); after load and on hover, document.getAnimations() has no running animation on transform and none longer than 150ms

a-lp-fallbacks.text: Design the opaque version first, then add glass. Without backdrop-filter support (@supports not (backdrop-filter: blur(1px))), or under prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce where browsers support it, panels become opaque tinted fills: #EAF4FF face, same rim, edges and spill. Ship -webkit-backdrop-filter alongside for older Safari. Under prefers-contrast: more, drop sheen and glow behind text and strengthen rims to solid #0A43B0. In forced-colors mode, keep a real 1px transparent border on panels and pills so the system draws their edges.

test.spec: screenshot with backdrop-filter disabled and again with prefers-contrast: more emulated; all text still meets a-lp-contrast-pairs thresholds and panels still read as tinted slabs

perf-lp-backdrop.text: Backdrop blur is the page's most expensive effect: the browser re-reads and re-blurs whatever lies behind each blurred element whenever that content changes (scrolling, animation, video), and the cost grows with blurred area and radius. Budget: at most 3 live-blurred elements in any viewport (the nav plus one or two hero panels), radius 20px or less, never animate the blur radius, never blur over video or continuously animating content, and no live blur on cards in scrolling grids (use tint, edges and spill, or a pre-blurred backdrop image).

test.spec: in a headless browser at 1440x900 and 390x844, at each scroll stop count elements in the viewport whose computed backdrop-filter is not 'none'; must be <= 3

perf-lp-paint.text: Large blurred box-shadows, filter: blur() on many elements and animated gradients are expensive to repaint. Paint big glows and caustic pools once (radial-gradient backgrounds or a pre-rendered image), animate only transform and opacity, and on elements that move keep shadow blur radii at 80px or less with few stacked layers.

perf-lp-media.text: The hero scene is usually the LCP element: serve it as AVIF or WebP with srcset (about 300KB or less at desktop width), set width and height, preload it, and keep LCP at 2.5s or less (the Core Web Vitals 'good' threshold). Render the hero object into the image or as a light layered image, not WebGL, unless the product justifies it (q-lp-hero-media).

sig-lp-blue-fills.text: On-style: every translucent fill is blue-hued (hue about 205-228, as in pal-material-blue), from the faintest plate to the deepest rim; only the thin top-sheen layer is white. Off-style: neutral white or grey rgba fills, such as rgba(255,255,255,x) or rgba(0,0,0,x), as the panel body; cyan, teal or violet tints.

test.spec: read computed background colors and gradient stops of panels, nav and pills; excluding the top-sheen layer, every stop with alpha > 0.05 has hue 205-230 and saturation >= 50%

sig-lp-depth-variation.text: On-style: each translucent surface shows at least two tint densities (the face paler than the rim), and overlaps read deeper than either layer. Off-style: one flat alpha per card, identical everywhere.

test.spec: in a screenshot, on every panel a pixel within 6px of the lower rim is at least 8 L* darker than the face center; where two panels overlap, the overlap is at least 5 L* darker than the darker single layer

sig-lp-tinted-shadows.text: On-style: shadows beneath translucent objects are blue spill, and contact shadows are core blue at low alpha. Off-style: black or grey drop shadows above 0.2 alpha.

sig-lp-tinted-whites.text: On-style: page and section backgrounds are blue-tinted whites (hue about 205-220, lightness 93-99%); pure #FFFFFF appears only in small specular highlights and in text on deep blue. Off-style: a pure white page with color added on top.

test.spec: flag background or background-color set to #fff, #ffffff or white on html, body, main or section selectors: (background(-color)?)\s*:\s*(#fff(fff)?|white)\b (case-insensitive)

sig-lp-no-os-chrome.text: On-style: the light-through-glass relationship in original shapes. Off-style: anything recognizable as operating-system chrome or a rights-held asset: window title bars, minimize/maximize/close buttons, a Start orb, a taskbar, macOS traffic-light buttons, Microsoft or Apple logos, Windows wallpapers, the Bliss hill.

test.spec: the page contains no window title bars or caption buttons, Start orb, taskbar, traffic-light buttons, OS or brand logos, Windows wallpapers or a recreation of the Bliss photograph
